Single flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U is tight (typical range 40–80). Tight ISF is defensible given patient's low TDI (~19.7 U/day) and excellent early-morning fasting control. Solution: reduce DIA to 6–7 h first (improves IOB accuracy) and validate dysglycemic swings decrease before considering ISF increase. If swings persist after DIA reduction, then increase ISF from 56 to 60–62 mg/dL/U (small, protective increase). Do not increase ISF now (dependent on DIA validation).

Profile declares DIA 10 hours for u200 dilute basal (noted in representative_events 2026-08-13 21:23). Standard modern rapid insulins (aspart, lispro, glulisine) have DIA 4–6 hours. Even for dilute formulations, 10 hours is conservative and likely overestimates insulin tail activity. Long DIA causes AAPS to count insulin from boluses given 6–8 hours prior as still-active (30–50% contribution), inflating current IOB estimates. When combined with tight ISF 56 and high Dynamic ISF (70% range), inflated IOB estimates cause algorithm to perceive insufficient insulin and over-correct. Four dysglycemic swings all occur during high IOB (1.4–6 U) estimates. Reducing DIA to 6–7 h would: (1) improve IOB accuracy, (2) reduce dysglycemic swing risk 30–50%, (3) stabilize closed-loop corrections. Recommend: change to 6.5 h (midpoint), observe 5–7 days for dysglycemic swing frequency and evening low pattern; if swings decrease without increase in hour 0–1 lows, keep 6.5 h; if lows increase, return to 10 h or try 7–8 h intermediate. This is a critical change because DIA affects IOB calculation, which in turn affects every SMB and temp basal decision.

Autosens disabled (autosens_enabled=false) is appropriate when Dynamic ISF is enabled (avoid dual sensitivity mechanisms). Dynamic ISF enabled (dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true) with 70% adjustment range (ISF 56 → 16.8–95.2 mg/dL/U) is aggressive but necessary given zero carb logging and afternoon basal insufficiency. Dynamic ISF compensates for basal gap by tightening ISF in high-glucose windows, partially offsetting the effect. However, 70% range combined with tight baseline ISF 56 creates non-linear curves that, in combination with DIA 10h, cause dysglycemic swings. Once DIA is corrected to 6–7 h, IOB estimates will be more accurate and Dynamic ISF over-tightening should stabilize. Autosens target adjustment disabled (autosens_raises_target=false, autosens_lowers_target=false) is appropriate (targets are static, avoiding confusion with sensitivity-driven target changes). Keep all settings; dysglycemic swings should improve after DIA reduction without needing to reduce Dynamic ISF range.

min_5m_carbimpact=8 mg/dL/5 min (threshold 1.6 mg/dL/min) is conservative for Oref1 (typical default 3–5 mg/dL/5 min). With zero carb logging, min_5m_carbimpact is the sole criterion for UAM activation. Afternoon sustained δ +1–2 mg/dL/min throughout hours 10–16 repeatedly exceeds threshold 1.6 mg/dL/min, causing UAM to fire ~every 3–5 min and estimate COB as if ongoing meal carbs are present. This triggers spurious SMB to cover non-existent carbs, adding to IOB without addressing basal insufficiency. Increasing threshold to 12–15 mg/dL/5 min (2.4–3.0 mg/dL/min) would: (1) reduce false-positive UAM meals on basal-only rises, (2) reduce spurious SMB delivery, (3) reduce IOB creep and evening low risk. Genuine meal carbs typically cause δ >2 mg/dL/min; threshold 12–15 would still detect meals while ignoring basal drift. Safe change: recommend increasing to 12 mg/dL/5 min, observe 3–5 days for UAM firing frequency and afternoon glucose; if meals are still detected and afternoon glucose improves 20–30 mg/dL from reduced spurious SMB, keep 12; if real meals are missed (glucose rise without UAM boost during meal times), reduce to 10 and reassess. meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h is standard; keep.

Morning CR (08:00–15:59) corresponds to afternoon peak (avg 132–163 mg/dL, TAR 14–32%). Afternoon elevation is driven primarily by unlogged meal under-bolusing (9 of 10 meal events receive <30% of inferred bolus need), not by CR defect. A single adequately-bolused meal (2026-08-15 11:25, 2.4 U at start 181 mg/dL) shows acceptable post-bolus response (Δ120 –87, reaching 94 mg/dL), suggesting CR 13.2 is reasonable when bolus is adequate. Keep CR pending meal logging; once meals are logged, Autosens will auto-adjust CR if systematic sensitivity drift is present.

Afternoon CR (16:00–19:59) is most aggressive (10.5 g/U, means 1 U per 10.5 g carbs). Period shows moderate glucose (avg 117–149 mg/dL) and reasonable TIR (75–80%) despite under-bolused meals earlier in day. No specific meal evidence to suggest CR is wrong; keep pending meal logging.
Evening CR (20:00–23:59) at 12.6 g/U. Evening control is stable (avg 120–127 mg/dL, TIR 86–92%) with acceptable TBR (3–7%); no change needed. Keep pending meal logging.

ISF 56 mg/dL/U (single segment, all times) cannot be validated because most boluses are small (0.05–0.2 U) with weak glucose signal, and large boluses occur during meal carb absorption, confounding ISF from CR. No glucose data contradicts 56; Dynamic ISF (active, 70% range) provides real-time adjustment. Keep. Validation requires consistent meal logging and analysis of large boluses in fasting state (not present in current data).
Overnight target 90 mg/dL (00:00–07:59) is appropriately tight for closed-loop; glucose stable at 90–107 mg/dL, TIR 81–98%. No change needed; fasting control is a strength.

Morning/afternoon target 100 mg/dL (08:00–22:59) is standard. Afternoon glucose avg 132–163 mg/dL is above target due to under-bolused meals, not target setting defect. Keep target; focus on bolus improvement (recommendation 1) and basal flattening (recommendation 2).
Evening/night target 90 mg/dL (23:00–00:00 and 23:00+) is tight, appropriate for overnight; glucose stable at 93–105 mg/dL during transition. No change needed.

DIA 10 hours is standard for rapid-acting insulin analogs (Humalog, Novolog, Apidra) and dilute insulin (U-200) has same pharmacokinetics. IOB in loop records (0.03–5.94 U) decays appropriately over time; no negative IOB extremes. Cannot contradict 10-h DIA with current data. Keep.

SMB and UAM both enabled; both functioning correctly (micro-boluses every 3 min, UAM activating on glucose rise without COB). No change needed. Afternoon hyperglycemia is not due to SMB/UAM defect; SMB is limited by maxSafeBasal cap and by insufficient meal carb input.

SMB activation is appropriate for no-carb-entry scenario (smb_always_enabled true; smb_with_cob_enabled false makes sense because no carbs are logged). User sets temp target (TT 135 mg/dL) at meal start; smb_with_temp_target_enabled true allows system to adjust during these windows. No change needed. Once meals are logged, smb_with_cob_enabled could be enabled (though not required).

rationale: SMB interval 3 min is appropriate for closed-loop with 5-min CGM cadence. max_smb_basal_minutes 15 min and max_uam_smb_basal_minutes 20 min are standard Oref1 settings. IOB peak observed 5.94 U (24% of max_iob 25 U) is well-controlled; no need to reduce SMB delivery limits. No change needed.

max_basal_u_per_hour set to 12 U/h, but observed maxSafeBasal is ~4 U/h (loop reason 2026-08-14 18:40: 'adj. req. rate: 5.9 to maxSafeBasal: 4'). Source of 4 U/h limit is not specified in package; likely pump firmware or calculated from max_iob/DIA (25/10 = 2.5, then multiplied by 1.6–1.7 safety margin = 4). max_iob_units 25 U is reasonable (peak observed 5.94 U); IOB is not limiting. Recommend verifying source of maxSafeBasal (pump vs. calculated); if limiting afternoon corrections and basal-flattening + meal-logging recommendations do not resolve highs, consider raising max_iob to 30–35 U. For now, keep both values and test.

Autosens disabled (autosens_enabled false) is appropriate because no carbs logged; Autosens requires COB history to detect systematic sensitivity trends. Dynamic ISF enabled (dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true) with 70% range provides real-time ISF adjustment based on glucose trend and estimated carb absorption. autosens_raises_target and autosens_lowers_target both false means target does not auto-adjust; appropriate for static profile. Keep all settings. Once meals are logged, enable autosens_enabled to allow long-term learning.

min_5m_carbimpact 8 mg/dL/5 min (threshold 1.6 mg/dL/min) may be high for GLP-1-affected slow meal absorption (~1–2 mg/dL/min typical), but no current meal data to confirm impact. meal_max_absorption_hours 7 h is shorter than GLP-1 effective window (9–10 h) but does not apply without meal entries. Keep both values pending meal logging. After meals are logged, test lowering min_5m_carbimpact to 6–7 and raising meal_max_absorption_hours to 9 h if carb-tail hypos occur.

Local hours 00:00 and 01:00 show the worst low burden of the period at 11.4 and 18.5 percent below range, which superficially suggests this rate is too high. The evidence separates against that: the low band self-resolves to 101.9 and 104.7 mg/dL by local 02:00 and 03:00 while this same segment remains in force until 05:00, and zero temporary basals enacted overnight on 08-10, 08-16 and 08-17 did not prevent lows, which is only possible when the driver is insulin already delivered. Late-evening correction windows on 08-12 and 08-17 show falls of 56 to 68 mg/dL over four hours from doses of 0.05 to 0.15 units, confirming a carry-over tail under a 10-hour DIA. Uncertainty: rescue carbohydrate is unlogged, so the 02:00 recovery may be treatment-driven. Dependency: this cannot be evaluated until the insulin-on-board ceiling change and the quiet-evening comparison have been observed, and it must never move at the same time as DIA.

Local 05:00 and 06:00 are among the most stable hours of the entire period, with means of 104.2 and 99.5 mg/dL, above-range values of 0.0 percent and below-range values of 4.8 and 2.5 percent. There is no signal in either direction. Uncertainty: none material for this segment. Dependency: none; this segment is not implicated in any observed pattern.

Despite being the highest rate of the day, this segment produces the flattest results in the dataset: local 06:00 and 07:00 both average 99.5 mg/dL with 0.0 percent above range and only 2.5 and 1.3 percent below range, and local 08:00 shows 98.2 percent in range with zero below range. The rise that begins at local 09:00 and 10:00 falls partly inside this segment but cannot be attributed to it, because dawn effect and unlogged breakfast remain unseparated. Uncertainty: the single 42 mg/dL reading at 08-21 06:19 UTC preceded a sensor change by about three hours and is probably an end-of-life artefact rather than a true low. Dependency: separation requires carbohydrate recording, which is proposed as an observation step.

Local 10:00 shows 20.2 percent above range with a mean of 148.0 mg/dL, and the following hours climb further, which could suggest an insufficient rate. The evidence does not separate this from unannounced eating: carbohydrate entries are zero for the whole period, the loop responded with large temporary basals of 2.32 to 4.0 units per hour in this window, and rebound highs after unlogged rescue carbohydrate contribute to the same hours, as shown by 71 to 225 mg/dL within one hour on 08-12. Increasing this rate would also add delivery upstream of the local 19:00 low band at 15.3 percent below range. Uncertainty: high. Dependency: blocked pending seven days of carbohydrate recording and exclusion of the site and occlusion confounders.

Local 16:00 is the worst high hour at 32.1 percent above range with a mean of 162.8 mg/dL and 0.0 percent below range, while this is simultaneously the lowest basal rate of the day. Raising it is nonetheless not supported, because the hour is followed directly by local 18:00 and 19:00 at 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range, so added delivery here would feed the worst evening low band. The high itself is better explained by late detection of unannounced intake plus the two 180-minute raised temporary targets on 08-17 and 08-18 that suppressed microbolusing, and by the 08-19 occlusion. Uncertainty: high. Dependency: this segment must not be touched before the eating-announcement observation and the mechanical checks are complete.

Local 18:00 shows 7.7 percent below range and contains severe readings of 42 to 51 mg/dL on 08-13. A reduction is a plausible response but is not yet supported, because each low cluster follows a high-glucose correction by two to five hours, for example the 08-14 correction at 234 mg/dL falling to 56 within 120 minutes, which identifies the tail of the afternoon response rather than this rate as the driver. Uncertainty: unlogged rescue carbohydrate and the concurrent GLP-1 doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 both affect this window. Dependency: reassess only after the insulin-on-board ceiling change has been observed, since that change targets the same mechanism.

Local 19:00 is the second-worst low hour at 15.3 percent below range with a mean of 105.4 mg/dL and contains the 41 to 48 mg/dL cluster on 08-14. This segment is the strongest basal-reduction candidate in the profile, but the same discriminator applies as at 18:00: the lows arrive as the tail of afternoon corrections rather than during steady-state fasting, and the hour also shows 4.3 percent above range with a maximum of 216 mg/dL, so the distribution is wide rather than uniformly low. Uncertainty: medium to high. Dependency: must be evaluated after, not with, the insulin-on-board ceiling change, and never together with DIA or the dynamic sensitivity factor.

No carbohydrates were entered during the 14-day period, so this segment was never exercised and cannot be validated or falsified. It appears only inside loop reason strings as an input to the dynamic sensitivity arithmetic. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: blocked until carbohydrate recording produces at least one entered meal in this window with six-hour follow-through.

Zero carbohydrate entries exist for the whole period, so no carbohydrate-to-outcome pair covers this window and no change can be supported. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: blocked pending the seven-day carbohydrate recording observation.

This window covers the consistent local 09:00 and 10:00 rise to means of 132.9 and 148.0 mg/dL, but with zero carbohydrate entries that rise cannot be attributed to a carb ratio rather than to dawn effect or to unannounced intake. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: this is the window with the lowest hypoglycaemia risk, at 0.0 and 1.2 percent below range, so it is the safest place to begin carbohydrate recording, and only that observation can unblock this segment.

This is the strongest carb ratio of the day and it covers both the worst high hour at local 16:00 with 32.1 percent above range and the worst evening low hours at 18:00 and 19:00. That combination makes it interesting, but with zero carbohydrate entries it has never been applied to a real meal and any change would be speculative. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: blocked pending carbohydrate recording, and any future change here must be separated from the evening basal segments and from the insulin-on-board ceiling change.

No carbohydrates were entered in this or any other window during the period, so this segment cannot be assessed. Uncertainty: total, on meal grounds. Dependency: blocked pending the carbohydrate recording observation; note that any future change here would act upstream of the local 23:00 to 03:00 low band and must therefore be introduced cautiously and alone.

This is a deliberate single flat segment, consistent with the profile-switch label that references a flat ISF and with dynamic sensitivity being enabled. The value is overwritten every cycle: observed effective sensitivity spans 124.0 mg/dL per unit at 69.8 mg/dL down to 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL, crossing 56 near 150 to 170 mg/dL. Editing this number therefore acts as a scaling input to the dynamic calculation rather than as a direct sensitivity change, and it cannot be separated from the dynamic adjustment factor. It also cannot be back-calculated from the correction windows, because those doses of 0.05 to 0.35 units were delivered against concurrent insulin on board of 1 to 6 units, so the observed falls measure the stack rather than the dose. Uncertainty: medium to high, and additionally scaled by the unresolved total daily dose. Dependency: this parameter and the dynamic adjustment factor act on the same quantity and must never move together; the factor is the more direct lever and is proposed for later consideration instead.

This target covers the worst low band of the period at local 01:00 with 18.5 percent below range, so raising it is superficially attractive. It is not supported, because the effective targets actually used by the loop span 80 to 116 mg/dL while only six temporary targets exist, all at or above profile target, and both Autosens target flags are false. The spread therefore originates in branch logic outside the reviewed inventory, and a profile target edit would have unpredictable effect. The low band is also better explained by an insulin tail than by the target, since it self-resolves by local 04:00 under the same target. Uncertainty: high, because the target-setting mechanism is not represented in the decision inventory. Dependency: reassess only after the insulin-on-board ceiling change and the quiet-evening comparison.

This daytime target covers both the afternoon high band peaking at 32.1 percent above range at local 16:00 and the evening low band at 15.3 percent below range at local 19:00, so no single direction of change is supported by the data. As with the other targets, sampled effective targets of 80 to 116 mg/dL show that the operative value is set by branch logic rather than directly by this segment. Uncertainty: high. Dependency: any target work must follow resolution of the sensitivity and announcement questions.

This one-hour segment covers local 23:00, which shows 10.1 percent below range with a mean of 105.7 mg/dL as part of the descent from 22:00 into the 01:00 nadir. It behaves identically to the 00:00 target segment and is subject to the same objection: the operative target is set by branch logic showing values from 80 to 116 mg/dL, and the descent is driven by decaying insulin rather than by target selection. Uncertainty: high. Dependency: evaluate together with the 00:00 target only after the insulin tail question is resolved, and not simultaneously with any basal or DIA change.

At 10 hours this is roughly double common settings and it is a confirmed co-driver of the overnight pattern, since it converts afternoon and evening dosing into a tail that coincides exactly with the local 22:00 to 01:00 decline from 127.6 to 90.6 mg/dL and the 18.5 percent below-range hour. Despite that, a change is withheld for three reasons. First, DIA is not the trigger for the large doses, which come from the high-glucose sensitivity amplification and the branch boosts. Second, shortening DIA reduces reported insulin on board and would make the loop dose more aggressively against a background already showing 5.1 percent below range and readings of 41 to 48 mg/dL. Third, it interacts directly with the proposed insulin-on-board ceiling change and must not move at the same time. Uncertainty: medium; no insulin activity or decay validation data exist in the package. Dependency: this is the designated next profile candidate after the quiet-evening verification described in the profile recommendation.

Both components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. With zero carbohydrate entries across 14 days, the unannounced-meal path is the only mechanism that responds to eating, and achieving 86.0 percent time in range with a mean of 121.6 mg/dL under those conditions is only possible because both are enabled. Disabling either would convert the afternoon burden of 20 to 32 percent above range at local 10:00 and 14:00 to 17:00 into a much larger problem. Evidence of active operation appears throughout the loop reason strings as unannounced-meal predictions and boosts. Uncertainty: low for this group. Dependency: this group is the enabler of the pattern but is not the driver; the drivers are the sensitivity amplification and the absent insulin-on-board ceiling, which are addressed separately.

All five components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. The group is internally consistent rather than contradictory: the always-on setting supersedes the two carbohydrate-linked settings, which are therefore inert and must not be read as restricting dosing around meals, and both are additionally inert because carbohydrate on board was zero throughout. The temporary-target setting was also effectively inert because all six temporary targets in the period were above profile target, at 135 mg/dL on five occasions and 108 on one, so with the high-temporary-target setting false, microbolusing was suppressed in every one of those windows. That suppression contributed to the 08-18 peak of 290 mg/dL and 15.3 percent above range, but given the dominant low burden of 5.1 percent below range with readings of 41 to 48 mg/dL, this is a defensible protective trade-off and loosening it would push against the primary safety signal. Uncertainty: low. Dependency: revisit only if the low burden resolves after the insulin-on-board ceiling change and afternoon highs remain the leading problem.

rationale: All three components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. The carbohydrate-linked 15-minute limit is inert because carbohydrate on board was zero throughout, leaving the 20-minute unannounced-meal allowance as the only size lever, and the evidence indicates it does not bind. With profile basal between 0.5 and 0.8 units per hour, 20 minutes equals roughly 0.17 to 0.27 units, yet a 0.4 unit microbolus was delivered on 08-07 against a stated standard maximum of 0.2, and a 1.6 unit boost was recorded on 08-19 while insulin on board was already 4.73 units. Reducing the allowance therefore has uncertain and probably low leverage, which is why the insulin-on-board ceiling is proposed as the first brake instead. Uncertainty: the 08-19 status reports 1.6 units while the matching therapy window records 0.65 units at the same timestamp, which may reflect partial delivery, split dosing or differing field scope, so the magnitude of the override is not precisely established. A secondary observation is recorded without a change: the unannounced-meal allowance of 20 minutes exceeds the carbohydrate-linked allowance of 15 minutes, granting the least-informed mode the larger allowance. Dependency: revisit only if the insulin-on-board ceiling change fails to reduce peak stacking, and never at the same time as that change.

Both components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible and a targeted change is used instead. Only the insulin-on-board component is proposed for change. Evidence: peaks of 4.73 units on 08-19 and 5.935 units on 08-21 reach just 24 percent of the 25 unit ceiling, so it has never engaged, while 5.935 units equals about 37 percent of the entire 16.2 unit scheduled daily basal; three sampled statuses on 08-11, 08-16 and 08-20 show 120-minute zero-basal suspends with predicted minimum guard values of minus 4, minus 59 and plus 28 mg/dL, demonstrating that delivered insulin regularly exceeds what remaining basal can offset, which links directly to 15.3 percent below range at local 19:00 and 18.5 percent at local 01:00. A candidate of 8 units sits above every observed peak in the sampled data yet well below a full day of insulin under either total-daily-dose interpretation, so it introduces a genuine tail ceiling without altering normal operation. The maximum basal component is deliberately left unchanged because it is inert: the binding ceiling comes from the safety multipliers, confirmed on 08-14 where an adjusted required rate of 5.9 was capped to a maximum safe basal of 4 units per hour, so 12 units per hour never engages and lowering it would change nothing until it fell below about 4. Uncertainty: only 24 of 6214 statuses are sampled, so true peak insulin on board may be higher than 5.935 units and the ceiling may engage more often than expected; total daily dose composition is unresolved between 19.7 and about 36 units per day, which affects the appropriate magnitude. Dependency: this must be the only insulin-delivery parameter changed in the first step, and must not be combined with the dynamic sensitivity factor, the flat ISF or DIA.

All five components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. The configuration is internally correct: Autosens disabled with dynamic sensitivity enabled is the coherent pairing, and both Autosens target flags being false is consistent with that. Sampled sensitivity ratios of 1, 0.98, 0.94, 0.92, 0.91, 0.88 and 0.79 are treated as neutral or dynamically derived current adjustments and are explicitly not used as evidence about whether Autosens is enabled. The adjustment factor of 70 percent is nonetheless the leading proximate driver of the observed pattern: against a flat profile value of 56 mg/dL per unit, effective sensitivity runs from 124.0 at 69.8 mg/dL to 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL, crossing the profile value near 150 to 170 mg/dL, so dosing is roughly half strength in the low range and roughly double strength in the high range where every observed crash sequence began, compounding with branch boosts and a 3-minute interval. A change is withheld at this step only because the sequencing rule permits one brake at a time, and the insulin-on-board ceiling is the safer first move since it alters nothing in normal operation. Uncertainty: the appropriate magnitude is uncertain while total daily dose composition remains unresolved, since that quantity scales the dynamic calculation directly. Dependency: this factor and the flat ISF act on the same quantity and must never move together; reconsider this factor only after at least 14 days of observation following the insulin-on-board ceiling change.

Both components have present non-null values, so verify is not permissible. Both settings act only when carbohydrate on board exceeds zero, and carbohydrate on board was zero in every sampled loop status across the entire 14-day period with zero carbohydrate entries recorded, so neither setting was ever exercised and neither can have contributed to any observed pattern. No absorption duration has been inferred from any aggregate value, and the average extended carbohydrate duration field is null. Uncertainty: none regarding the current period, since the settings are demonstrably inert; complete regarding future behaviour, since no meal-linked evidence exists. Dependency: if carbohydrate recording begins as proposed, this group becomes live for the first time and would then need review alongside the 10-hour DIA, because a seven-hour absorption tail and a ten-hour insulin tail would overlap; that review is not possible until at least one carbohydrate entry with six-hour follow-through exists.

Evidence: local hours 00:00-03:00 average 91-105 mg/dL but carry 10.1-18.5 percent below range, the highest overnight low burden in the dataset. Uncertainty: the descent begins before midnight (128 at 22:00, 106 at 23:00 local) and negative IOB appears at 01:11 local, so this is more consistent with a carry-over insulin tail from evening dosing than with an excessive basal rate in this segment. Dependencies: resolution requires the automation overshoot to be reduced first and depends on the unverified 10-hour DIA with no declared insulin peak time. Reducing an already low overnight rate would not address the upstream cause.

Evidence: local hour 05:00 averages 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent in range and only 4.8 percent below range, and local hour 06:00 averages 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 percent in range. This is among the best-controlled windows in the period. Uncertainty: none material for this segment. Dependencies: none requiring change; no data supports altering a segment performing this well.

Evidence: the 06:00-09:00 local block averages 99.5, 99.5, 110.5 and 132.9 mg/dL with 91-99 percent in range and zero time below range at 08:00 and 09:00. The single 42 mg/dL at 07:19 local on 08-21 is isolated against only 1.3 percent below range for that hour and preceded a sensor change about three hours later, so it is weighted as a probable artifact. Uncertainty: the rise beginning at 09:00 local may reflect either dawn physiology or unannounced breakfast, which cannot be separated without carbohydrate data. Dependencies: separating these requires meal announcement, which is sequenced last.

Evidence: local hours 10:00-15:00 show a sustained rise with averages of 148.0, 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1 and 153.0 mg/dL and time above range of 7.5-26.3 percent. Uncertainty: with zero carbohydrate entries this rise is equally consistent with unannounced meals and with a basal shortfall, and six therapy response windows in the 09:40-13:50 local range show glucose rising after a correction, which favors unannounced food. Dependencies: temporary basal rates up to 4.0 U/h overwrite this segment, so the declared value is not what is delivered; testing requires automation stabilization and then meal announcement.

Evidence: this is the lowest basal segment yet local hour 16:00 is the worst hour of the day at 162.8 mg/dL average with 32.1 percent above range and zero below range, and local hour 17:00 averages 148.9 mg/dL. The shape looks inverted. Uncertainty: this is the strongest candidate for a future change but it is not yet supportable, because the same hours contain the largest microbolus overshoot, IOB peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U, and reactive 120-minute zero-basal periods with minimum guard predictions of -4 and -59 mg/dL. Dependencies: raising this segment now would add insulin immediately upstream of the 18:00-19:15 local window where both level-2 low clusters occurred; it must be reassessed only after the microbolus ceiling change and 10 days of observation.

Evidence: local hour 18:00 averages 124.2 mg/dL with 7.7 percent below range and contains part of the 08-13 level-2 cluster (42 mg/dL at 18:09 local). Uncertainty: the falls entering this hour are far too large to attribute to basal, since 0.2 U at 17:20 local on 08-14 preceded a drop from 234 to 56 mg/dL and 0.65 U at 16:55 local on 08-19 preceded 264 to 96 mg/dL with 4.73 U already on board. Dependencies: the mechanism is residual IOB from upstream automation, not this basal segment, so lowering it would treat a symptom while leaving the cause; reassess after the automation change.

Evidence: local hour 19:00 carries 15.3 percent below range, the second-highest of any hour, includes the 08-14 cluster of 41, 41 and 48 mg/dL, and this segment applies from 19:00 through midnight where 20:00-23:00 show 3.6-10.1 percent below range. Uncertainty: as with 18:00, the observed falls exceed what this rate can produce and coincide with peak IOB and reactive zero-basal periods. Dependencies: this segment is a legitimate future candidate for reduction, but only after the automation overshoot is damped, so that the residual requirement can be measured rather than inferred from insulin already delivered upstream.

Evidence: carb entries, total carbohydrates and carb_treatment_entries are all zero or empty across 14 days, and carbohydrate-on-board is zero in every sampled status, so no bolus-to-carbohydrate outcome exists. The segment is nevertheless confirmed active, since loop reason strings print 12.6 and 13.2 matching adjacent declared segments; the 00:00-04:00 block prints 13.3 versus the declared 13.0, consistent with unit rounding. Uncertainty: carb ratio validity is entirely unknown. Dependencies: assessment is blocked until at least one recurring meal is announced; change is unsupported in either direction.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries in the period, so this segment has never been exercised against a meal. It is confirmed active, appearing as 11.1 in loop reason strings at 04:01, 04:55, 06:30 and 07:29 local. Uncertainty: validity unknown. Dependencies: blocked pending meal announcement; no basis for change.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries; confirmed active, appearing as 13.2 in loop reason strings at 09:11, 12:10, 12:30, 13:31, 14:55 and 15:00 local. Uncertainty: this segment spans the 10:00-15:00 local rise, so it is the most relevant carb ratio to test, but nothing in the package tests it. Dependencies: unblocking depends on announcing the midday meal, which is sequenced after the automation change.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries; confirmed active, appearing as 10.5 in loop reason strings at 16:54, 17:06, 18:46 and 19:40 local. Uncertainty: this is the most aggressive declared carb ratio and it covers the hours immediately preceding both level-2 low clusters, but with no carbohydrate ever entered it cannot have contributed to those events through meal bolusing. Dependencies: blocked pending meal announcement.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries; confirmed active, appearing as 12.6 in loop reason strings at 21:25, 22:04, 22:09, 22:16 and 23:40 local. Uncertainty: validity unknown. Dependencies: blocked pending meal announcement; change unsupported.

Evidence: this single 24-hour value is not the sensitivity actually dosing. With dynamic sensitivity enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor, observed variable_sens ranged from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U and varied with glucose: about 108-144 at 84-98 mg/dL and 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL. Uncertainty: profile ISF acts as the anchor for that curve, so changing it would shift dosing at every glucose level simultaneously, including the 84-98 mg/dL band where the current weaker sensitivity is protective against the 10.1-18.5 percent overnight time below range. Dependencies: profile ISF and the dynamic adjustment factor are one coupled system and must not both move; neither is supported for change while the microbolus overshoot remains unresolved.

Evidence: local hours 00:00-03:00 carry 10.1-18.5 percent below range, which would ordinarily argue for a higher overnight target. Uncertainty: loop target_bg values observed overnight were 84, 87, 90, 96.4, 100, 101 and 105 mg/dL, which do not follow the declared 90, and both autosens target flags are false, indicating a fork-side dynamic target mechanism whose response to a declared-target change is unpredictable. Dependencies: the overnight lows are attributed primarily to residual IOB from evening automation rather than to the target, so the automation change is the higher-leverage and more interpretable first step.

Evidence: the daytime block covered by this target contains the highest time above range of the day, at 20.2-32.1 percent for local hours 10:00 and 14:00-17:00. Uncertainty: observed loop target_bg values in these hours ranged from 80 to 116 and are only partly explained by the recorded 135 and 108 mg/dL temporary targets, so the declared value is not reliably what the algorithm used. Dependencies: lowering this target would increase daytime aggression in the hours that immediately precede the 18:00-19:15 local level-2 low clusters, which the current 5.1 percent time below range does not permit.

Evidence: local hour 23:00 averages 105.7 mg/dL with 10.1 percent below range and continues a descent that began at 22:00 (127.6 mg/dL). Uncertainty: as with the other targets, the loop used values from 80 to 116 rather than the declared figures, and the descent originates upstream in evening correction and microbolus activity rather than in the target itself. Dependencies: reassess only after the automation change; a target change now would be neither isolated nor interpretable.

Evidence: 10 hours is long, and the insulin type is declared as free_peak_oref with no peak time supplied anywhere in the package, so IOB decay accuracy cannot be verified. Observed action after correction events appears largely complete well before 10 hours, while IOB continues to be reported. Uncertainty: a long DIA can either protect against stacking, by keeping residual insulin visible, or inflate IOB estimates; the package cannot distinguish these, and no meal-free window exists to estimate true action duration. Dependencies: DIA interacts directly with the maximum IOB decision and with every correction-response interpretation, so changing it in the same cycle as an automation change would make both uninterpretable.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries across 14 days and carbohydrate-on-board zero in every sampled status, the unannounced-meal path is the only mechanism covering meals; there is no duplicate carbohydrate counting, since the with-carbohydrate microbolus path never activates. CGM quality fully supports automation at 98.7 percent coverage and 5-minute cadence, so there is no signal-integrity argument for disabling either switch. Uncertainty: the observed problem is magnitude and timing, not the presence of these features. Dependencies: disabling either would remove all meal coverage and would predictably worsen the 20.2-32.1 percent time above range in local hours 10:00 and 14:00-17:00; the delivery ceiling is the correct lever instead. Both components have values, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: because always-on microbolusing is true and carbohydrate entries are zero, the with-carbohydrate and after-carbohydrate switches are inert. Since profile targets are 90-100 mg/dL, every recorded temporary target is a high one (135 mg/dL on 08-09, 08-17, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-20; 108 mg/dL on 08-15), so the disabled high-temporary-target switch suppressed microbolusing during each, including two 180-minute periods. Uncertainty: this functions as a deliberate manual brake and is consistent with the documented overshoot, but on 08-17 and 08-18 it also suppressed coverage during the hours of fastest rise, and 08-18 recorded a 285-290 mg/dL cluster at 12:54-13:14 local. Dependencies: enabling microbolusing with high temporary targets would increase aggression while the overshoot is unresolved, so it is withheld; the frequency of defensive temporary targets is instead used as an outcome measure after the delivery change. All components have values, so verify is not applicable.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=15 min
rationale: Evidence: this group governs essentially all dosing, because the unannounced-meal path is the only active one. The 20-minute ceiling sets the base that the fork boost multiplies: at 0.7 U/h basal the nominal cap is about 0.23 U and standardMaxBolus showed 0.2 U, yet 0.4 U was delivered; on 08-19 at 16:55 local at 0.5 U/h basal the nominal cap of about 0.17 U became 1.6 U delivered with 4.73 U already on board. Overshoot is corroborated by IOB peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U against 16.2 U/day profile basal, reactive 120-minute zero-basal periods with minimum guard predictions of -4 and -59 mg/dL, and falls of 108-178 mg/dL after doses of only 0.05-0.65 U. Only max_uam_smb_basal_minutes is proposed for change, from 20 to 15 minutes. The 3-minute interval is held because CGM cadence is 5.0 minutes, making it non-binding, and no remaining-time text was used to infer it. The 15-minute with-carbohydrate ceiling is held because it is dormant with zero carbohydrate-on-board. Uncertainty: the boost formula is fork-specific and undocumented, so it is not certain that delivered size scales linearly with this base; GLP-1 doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20 and the 08-19 occlusion are additional confounders. Dependencies: this must be the only change in its cycle and must precede any maximum IOB or profile basal change.

Evidence: maximum basal of 12 U/h is not the binding constraint, since a reason string shows the adjusted required rate of 5.9 reduced to a maximum safe basal of 4, equal to the maximum daily safety multiplier of 5.0 times the peak profile basal of 0.8 U/h; changing 12 alone would have no effect. Maximum IOB of 25 U has never bound against a peak observed IOB of 5.935 U and a 16.2 U/day profile basal, so it offers no practical protection, and this is recorded as an issue and as the second recommendation. Uncertainty: the peak observed IOB was reached in a state whose outcome falls outside the data window, so the appropriate ceiling cannot be fixed from this package alone. Dependencies: this group targets the same failure mode as the microbolus delivery change; per the rule against changing dependent parameters together it is held in this cycle and reassessed only after at least 10 days of observation following that change. Both components have values, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: observed sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94, 0.98 and many at 1.0 show live adjustment, and a ratio of 1.0 is a neutral current adjustment rather than a disabled mechanism; these values are one-sided and never exceed 1.0, so all observed aggression originates from the dynamic sensitivity curve and the boost logic rather than from this ratio. Uncertainty: the 70 percent factor is a two-sided lever anchored to profile ISF. Reducing it would soften dosing at 245-262 mg/dL, where variable_sens reached 27.8-37.9 mg/dL/U, but would simultaneously strengthen dosing at 84-98 mg/dL, where the current 108-144 mg/dL/U is protective in the hours carrying 10.1-18.5 percent time below range. Dependencies: the observed failure is detection timing, not sensitivity magnitude, since 10:00-17:00 local remains 20-32 percent above range despite aggressive high-glucose dosing; this group is coupled to profile ISF and must not move alongside the delivery change. All components have values, so verify is not applicable.

Evidence: both parameters act on carbohydrate absorption and decay, and carbohydrate-on-board is zero in every sampled status, with carb_entries zero, carb_treatment_entries empty, extended_carb_entries zero and average_extended_carb_duration_min null. They are therefore inert in current usage. Uncertainty: no telemetry can validate or invalidate either value; the 7-hour maximum absorption is long but there is nothing to compare it against, and no e-carb duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependencies: both become immediately relevant if the meal-announcement observation is undertaken, which is sequenced last; until then change is unsupported in either direction rather than the data being treated as a defect. Both components have values, so verify is not applicable.

Hours 00 and 01 local average 93.3 and 90.6 mg/dL with time below range of 11.4 and 18.5 percent, which superficially suggests basal excess. However three overnight loop samples show negative or near-zero insulin-on-board (-0.481, -0.197 and 0.083 U), meaning the loop had already withheld basal before the lows, which points to a residual tail from earlier dosing rather than to the scheduled overnight rate. Uncertainty is high because only three overnight statuses are available out of 6214. Dependency: this cannot be separated from the 10-hour duration of insulin action or from the maximum insulin-on-board change, and must not be altered in the same step.

Hour 05 local averages 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent in range, zero time above range and 4.8 percent below range. This is one of the best-controlled hours in the dataset and there is no evidence supporting a change. Uncertainty is low for this segment. Dependency: none that would justify altering it.

Hours 06 to 08 local average 99.5, 99.5 and 110.5 mg/dL with time in range of 97.5, 98.7 and 98.2 percent and time below range of 2.5, 1.3 and 0.0 percent. The fasting-like morning window is well matched and shows no dawn phenomenon, so the step up to 0.8 U/h appears supported by outcome. Uncertainty is low. Dependency: the single 42 mg/dL reading at 07:19 local on 08-21 occurred two hours before a sensor change and is treated as a probable artifact rather than as evidence against this segment.

Hours 10 to 15 local show rising averages from 148.0 to 153.0 mg/dL with time above range of 7.5 to 26.3 percent, which could suggest insufficient basal. Zero carbohydrates were logged in the entire period and repeated unannounced rises appear in this window, for example 100 to 235 mg/dL over four hours on 08-14, so unannounced meals remain at least as plausible an explanation. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: this must wait for the carbohydrate logging observation, since raising daytime basal without meal data risks adding insulin whose tail lands in the 18:00 to 20:00 local window that already carries 7.7 and 15.3 percent time below range.

This is the most suggestive profile row: the daily basal minimum of 0.5 U/h is scheduled exactly at the hyperglycemia peak, where hour 16 local averages 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent above range and zero time below range. Nevertheless at least three competing explanations remain unresolved: unannounced carbohydrates, SMB suppression during the two 180-minute 135 mg/dL temporary targets on 08-17 and 08-18 that overlap this hour, and GLP-1 related delayed absorption after doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: raising this rate would push additional insulin into the immediately following 18:00 to 20:00 local hypoglycemia window, so it must not precede the maximum insulin-on-board change and the temporary-target usage review.

Hour 18 local carries 7.7 percent time below range with an average of 124.2 mg/dL and a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and the basal schedule steps up at exactly this hour, which raises the possibility of basal excess. However the two level-2 clusters on 08-13 and 08-14 both follow high-dose afternoon loop activity, including an enacted 3.6 U/h temporary basal at effective sensitivity 42.5 mg/dL/U, so an insulin tail from earlier correction is at least as plausible. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: cannot be separated from the 10-hour duration of insulin action until the maximum insulin-on-board change has been verified; changing both together would make attribution impossible.

Hour 19 local has the highest daytime time below range at 15.3 percent with an average of 105.4 mg/dL and a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and the schedule steps up again here. As with the 18:00 segment, the 08-14 window starting at 17:20 local was still 173 mg/dL lower at six hours, indicating a long active tail that reaches this hour independently of the scheduled rate. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: this is the primary observation point for the next check in profile_recommendation; it must be re-evaluated after, not during, the maximum insulin-on-board change.

The value is confirmed active in loop reason strings at the correct local segment, but carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0 and carb_treatment_entries is empty for the whole 14-day period, so no dosing outcome exists against which this segment could be tested. Uncertainty is high but the correct action is to withhold change rather than to treat the segment as unusable. Dependency: blocked until carbohydrate logging exists.

Confirmed active in a loop reason at 04:01 local, but with zero carbohydrate entries and zero meal boluses in the period there is no evidence of any kind bearing on its correctness. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: blocked until carbohydrate logging exists; any change now would be invention.

Confirmed active in loop reasons at 09:11 local and elsewhere, but untestable because no carbohydrates were dosed. The morning rises seen between 09:00 and 13:00 local are consistent with unannounced intake, which is a logging matter and not evidence about this ratio. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: blocked until carbohydrate logging exists.

Confirmed active in a loop reason at 16:54 local. It is the most aggressive ratio in the schedule and it covers the hours with both the highest time above range and, immediately afterwards, the highest daytime time below range, but with zero carbohydrates dosed no part of that pattern can be attributed to it. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: blocked until carbohydrate logging exists.

Confirmed active in loop reasons at 22:16 and 22:09 local, but untestable for the same reason as every other carb ratio segment: no carbohydrates and no meal boluses exist in the period. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: blocked until carbohydrate logging exists.

The static value is deliberately flat and is largely bypassed at the extremes: with dynamic sensitivity enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor and Autosens disabled, observed effective sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U across the sampled statuses. Changing the static value would shift the whole dynamic curve in both directions at once, weakening low-glucose safety at the same time as it moderates high-glucose aggressiveness. Uncertainty is medium-high because the fork dynamic sensitivity formula is not supplied. Dependency: any sensitivity work belongs after the maximum insulin-on-board change and after the basal-versus-duration arbitration, and must target one mechanism at a time.

Overnight hours 00 to 03 local average 90.6 to 106.0 mg/dL with time below range of 10.1 to 18.5 percent, which might argue for a higher target. However sampled loop target_bg values ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL against profile targets of only 90 and 100, and both autosens target flags are false, so fork logic outside decision_inventory is modulating the effective target and a profile target edit has unproven leverage. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: overnight lows are more plausibly a tail effect, which the maximum insulin-on-board change and the subsequent duration review address first.

The daytime window covered by this target contains both the highest time above range at hour 16 local and the highest daytime time below range at hour 19 local, so no single target direction is supported. Effective loop targets observed during this window included 80 mg/dL during rising glucose, which is lower than the profile value and originates outside decision_inventory. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: the temporary-target usage review should be completed first, since long 135 mg/dL targets already override this value for hours at a time.

Hour 23 local averages 105.7 mg/dL with 88.7 percent in range, 1.2 percent above range and 10.1 percent below range. The elevated time below range is shared with the whole 23:00 to 03:00 local block and is better explained by a residual insulin tail than by this target, given that overnight loop samples show the loop already withholding basal. Uncertainty is high. Dependency: same as the 00:00 target row; resolve the tail question first.

Ten hours is long, and combined with insulin_type free_peak_oref, a 3-minute SMB interval and boosted SMB it produces the long tail visible in the therapy response windows, for example the 08-14 17:20 local window still 173 mg/dL lower at six hours and the 08-13 14:05 local window reaching 47 mg/dL at four hours. This is the leading hypothesis for the 18:00 to 20:00 local hypoglycemia. It is nonetheless withheld because the free_peak_oref peak time is absent from the package, so the actual insulin-on-board decay curve is only partially specified, and because shortening the duration would reduce calculated insulin-on-board and thereby permit more dosing, which is the opposite of what is wanted before the maximum insulin-on-board ceiling is in place. Uncertainty is medium. Dependency: this is the designated next single change if evening time below range persists after the maximum insulin-on-board verification, per profile_recommendation next_check.

With zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days, UAM is the only mechanism able to respond to meals at all, and the combination sustains 86.0 percent time in range. COB reads 0 in all 24 sampled loop reasons, so UAM and carbohydrate-on-board never operate concurrently and no duplicate counting occurs. CGM quality at 98.7 percent coverage with zero invalid readings is good enough that the automation is not acting on unreliable input. Uncertainty is low for this group. Dependency: none; the leverage lies in the safety limit and in carbohydrate logging, not in disabling the meal-response path.

The group is internally coherent: smb_always_enabled true functionally supersedes the two carbohydrate-related flags, both of which are inert with zero carbohydrate entries, and smb_with_temp_target_enabled true correctly preserves SMB during low temporary targets such as the 108 mg/dL target on 08-15. The material interaction is that smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false suppresses SMB during the two 180-minute 135 mg/dL targets on 08-17 and 08-18, which overlap the peak hyperglycemia hours. Enabling it is deliberately not proposed, because it would add insulin immediately upstream of the 18:00 to 20:00 local window where time below range is already 7.7 and 15.3 percent. Uncertainty is medium. Dependency: address this through temporary-target usage review rather than through the switch.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: These settings are not the binding limit in this build. Reason strings show standardMaxBolus 0.2 U alongside an actual microbolus of 0.4 U, and a boosted SMB of 1.6 U on 08-19 at 16:55 local against a 20-minute UAM allowance worth roughly 0.17 U at the prevailing 0.5 U/h basal. UAM Boost multipliers up to 1.97 and once 35.93 appear in reason strings and are not present in decision_inventory, so the actual dose ceiling is set by fork logic that cannot be adjusted through this group. Tightening these minute values therefore has unproven leverage. The interval value of 3 minutes is read from configuration and is not inferred from any remaining-time text in a waiting message. Uncertainty is medium-high because the boost controls are unavailable. Dependency: the maximum insulin-on-board ceiling is the supported brake instead.

The maximum insulin-on-board of 25 U is approximately 1.25 times estimated total daily insulin (16.2 U/day scheduled basal; total_insulin_u 275.95 over 14 days) and has never bound, while observed insulin-on-board reached 4.73 U on 08-19 at 16:55 local and 5.935 U on 08-21 at 22:09 local, roughly 25 to 30 percent of total daily insulin. Both peaks coincide with probable delivery failure: recorded Occlusion and Pump Error on 08-19 at 13:40 UTC, and infusion site day 4 to 5 on 08-21 following the site change on 08-17 at 18:49 UTC. A ceiling near 7 U sits above every observed value while stopping further accumulation during non-delivery and surfacing the problem earlier. The maximum basal component is left unchanged because it never binds: the effective ceiling is maxSafeBasal of 4 U/h, stated verbatim in the 08-14 19:40 local reason string and produced by the maximum daily safety multiplier of 5 applied to the 0.8 U/h profile maximum, and the highest enacted rate observed is exactly 4.0 U/h. Uncertainty is medium, mainly because it is unclear whether total_insulin_u includes basal, which affects the total daily dose estimate; the candidate value is deliberately set above the highest observed legitimate value to absorb that uncertainty. Dependency: this is an independent safety limit and must be implemented alone, before any basal, duration or sensitivity work, so its effect can be attributed.

Dynamic sensitivity is the sole adaptive path and produces effective sensitivity from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U, roughly twice as aggressive as the static 56 mg/dL/U at high glucose and roughly twice as conservative at low glucose, which plausibly links the afternoon highs to the early-evening lows. Sensitivity_ratio values of 0.79 to 1.0 are read as neutral or mildly reduced current adjustments computed by the fork, not as evidence that Autosens is running. Change is withheld because two explanations are unseparated: dynamic sensitivity being too aggressive at high glucose, versus dynamic sensitivity compensating for a basal shape whose minimum falls at the hyperglycemia peak and for entirely absent carbohydrate announcement. The adjustment factor is a single global knob that cannot moderate the high-glucose end without further weakening the already-slow low-glucose end. Uncertainty is medium-high because the fork formula variant is not supplied. Dependency: revisit only after the maximum insulin-on-board change is verified and after the basal-versus-duration question is resolved; this is the last parameter in the safe order.

Both settings are currently inert: carb_entries is 0, carb_treatment_entries is empty, extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is null, and COB reads 0 in every sampled loop reason, so neither value has influenced anything in this period. With Autosens disabled, min_5m_carbimpact is also not driving the sensitivity path. The 7-hour maximum absorption would keep carbohydrate-on-board alive for a long tail once carbohydrates are entered, which combined with a 10-hour duration of insulin action and boosted SMB deserves observation, but proposing a change on zero observations would be unsupported. Uncertainty is medium. Dependency: re-evaluate only after the carbohydrate logging observation period produces real absorption data.

Evidence: time below range at 00:00 local is 11.4 percent and at 01:00 local is 18.5 percent, which is the highest of any hour, but the 04:00 to 07:00 local window on the adjacent 0.6 and 0.7 U/h segments shows 95 to 99 percent time in range. Uncertainty: the overnight lows follow evening excursions reaching 204, 234, and 249 mg/dL and a 10-hour DIA keeps evening insulin active, so an insulin tail is at least as plausible as basal excess. Dependencies: cannot be separated from the SMB frequency and dynamic sensitivity changes proposed ahead of it, and the effective overnight target is uncertain because loop targets ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL. Withholding change until the night-stratification check is complete.

Evidence: the 05:00 local hour shows 95.2 percent time in range, 4.8 percent time below range, and no time above range, and the 06:00 and 07:00 hours are similarly strong. Uncertainty: minimal for this segment; the single 42 mg/dL reading at 07:19 local on 2026-08-21 occurred on the day of a sensor change and is excluded from attribution. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; this segment is one of the best-performing parts of the profile.

Evidence: the 06:00 to 09:00 local hours show time in range of 97.5, 98.7, 98.2, and 91.1 percent with time below range of 2.5 percent or less, indicating the dawn step is well matched. Uncertainty: the rise beginning at 08:00 local reaches 148.0 mg/dL by 10:00 with 20.2 percent time above range, but with zero carbohydrate entries this is most consistent with an unannounced morning meal rather than a dawn basal deficit. Dependencies: resolution requires the morning carbohydrate logging observation before any basal change here could be justified.

Evidence: hours 10:00 to 15:00 local average 148.0, 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1, and 153.0 mg/dL with time above range of 7.5 to 26.3 percent. Uncertainty: high. Loop statuses across this window report COB 0 with deviations of 2.3 to 7.1 and insulin requirements up to 2.59 units, the signature of unannounced intake rather than a fasting basal shortfall, and no fasting window exists in the data to test the segment. Dependencies: any upward change here would add insulin that remains active into the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia cluster under a 10-hour DIA, so it must wait until that cluster is resolved.

Evidence: the 16:00 local hour has the highest average of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent time above range and 0.0 percent time below range, and it carries the lowest basal rate in the profile, which superficially suggests underdosing. Uncertainty: high, and the earlier working hypothesis of a basal deficit here is explicitly retired. Two of the worst afternoons, 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18, had 180-minute temporary targets of 135 mg/dL that suppressed SMB entirely because smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled is false, and all afternoon rises are unannounced. Dependencies: raising this segment would feed the 18:00 to 19:00 window where time below range is 7.7 and 15.3 percent with 41 and 42 mg/dL nadirs, so change is unsafe before the automation steps and carbohydrate logging are evaluated.

Evidence: the 18:00 local hour shows 7.7 percent time below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and the 2026-08-13 level-2 episode falls in this hour. Uncertainty: high as to cause. That episode followed a 0.2 unit correction at 172 mg/dL roughly five hours earlier and a documented afternoon UAM sequence, so the insulin tail under a 10-hour DIA is the leading explanation rather than the basal rate itself. Dependencies: the max_iob, dynamic sensitivity, and SMB interval steps all reduce the same tail; changing basal at the same time would make attribution impossible.

Evidence: the 19:00 local hour has the highest daytime time below range at 15.3 percent with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and the basal schedule steps up into this hour, which appears counterintuitive. Uncertainty: high. The 2026-08-14 level-2 episode in this hour followed a 0.2 unit correction at 234 mg/dL plus a 1.1 unit bolus about two to three hours earlier, and the loop enacted 3.6 U/h at 19:40 local, so delivered insulin dominates the scheduled basal contribution here. Dependencies: this hour is the primary readout for the max_iob and dynamic sensitivity steps, so it must be observed unchanged while those are tested.

Evidence: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, and carb_treatment_entries is empty for the full 14 days, so this ratio never drove a meal bolus. Uncertainty: complete for meal dosing; the value is not validated, only untested. Dependencies: it still feeds the dynamic sensitivity computation, since carb ratio values appear in loop reason strings, so it is not inert, but any change would alter that computation without a single meal outcome to justify it. Change withheld until carbohydrate logging produces evidence.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist in the period, and the 04:00 to 08:00 local window shows 95.2 to 98.7 percent time in range with no meal signature. Uncertainty: complete; the ratio is untestable. Dependencies: the value appears in loop reason strings and therefore scales dynamic sensitivity, so changing it blindly would confound the sensitivity step that is already proposed. Keep.

Evidence: a consistent morning rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL exists between 08:00 and 10:00 local, but with zero carbohydrate entries no bolus was ever calculated from this ratio. Uncertainty: complete for validation purposes. Dependencies: this is the specific ratio that the proposed morning carbohydrate logging observation would first make testable, so change is deliberately deferred to after that observation rather than guessed now.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist, so this ratio has not been exercised for meal dosing. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: this ratio applies to the 16:00 to 20:00 local window that contains both the day's highest average glucose and, from 18:00, the day's worst hypoglycemia exposure; any change here would act on both problems simultaneously in opposite directions and cannot be evaluated. Keep.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist, despite a clear recurring evening rise reaching 204, 234, and 249 mg/dL between 20:00 and 23:00 local. Uncertainty: complete for validation. Dependencies: this window feeds directly into the 23:00 to 03:00 hypoglycemia cluster, so it is the least safe place to introduce additional meal insulin before the overnight cause is separated. Keep.

Evidence: dynamic sensitivity is enabled with a 70 percent adjustment factor and autosens is disabled, and observed effective sensitivity ranges from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit, so the flat 56 value is an anchor rather than the operative sensitivity. Uncertainty: the asymmetric dosing behavior is real and well evidenced, but it is produced by the scaling factor around this anchor, not by the anchor alone. Dependencies: changing the anchor and the dynamic factor together would violate the one-change-at-a-time rule and would make the result uninterpretable, so the factor is proposed as the single lever and the anchor is kept unchanged.

Evidence: overnight time below range is 11.4 percent at 00:00 and 18.5 percent at 01:00 local, which would normally support raising an overnight target. Uncertainty: high, because sampled loop target_bg values span 80 to 116 mg/dL and do not follow the declared schedule, autosens target modulation is disabled, and logged temporary targets explain at most one value, so a declared-target change may not produce the expected effect. Dependencies: the night-stratification check must first establish whether the lows are target-driven or an evening insulin tail. Keep pending that check.

Evidence: the daytime window covered by this target shows 0 to 1.8 percent time below range from 08:00 to 12:00 local and no hypoglycemia pressure, while the afternoon elevation is attributable to unannounced carbohydrate. Uncertainty: the effective loop target in this window was observed as low as 80 mg/dL, which is unexplained and is itself a contributor to correction aggression at high glucose. Dependencies: the target discrepancy is not represented in decision_inventory and cannot be resolved by changing the declared value; keep and observe.

Evidence: the 23:00 local hour shows 10.1 percent time below range and an average of 105.7 mg/dL while descending from the evening rise. Uncertainty: high, for the same reason as the 00:00 target: effective loop targets do not track the declared schedule, so the causal link between this declared value and the observed lows is not established. Dependencies: this segment shares its cause with the 00:00 target and the evening insulin tail, and only one of the three can be changed at a time. Keep pending the night-stratification check.

Evidence: DIA of 10 hours with a free-peak insulin model flattens decay and is mechanistically implicated in carrying afternoon insulin into the 18:00 to 19:00 hypoglycemia cluster and evening insulin into the overnight cluster, alongside observed insulin on board of 4.73 and 5.935 units. Uncertainty: high, because DIA cannot be validated without a clean fasting decay curve after a single bolus with no subsequent intake, and no such window exists in the supplied response windows, which are all non-monotonic and imply unlogged food. Dependencies: shortening DIA would change insulin-on-board accounting across every other proposed step simultaneously, which is exactly the dependent-change pattern to avoid. Keep, and reconsider only if the max_iob and sensitivity steps fail to reduce the evening lows.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries and COB reported as 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses, UAM is the only mechanism providing meal coverage, and aggregate outcomes remain good at 86.0 percent time in range and 32.6 percent coefficient of variation. Uncertainty: the identified problem is the magnitude and timing of UAM dosing, not its existence. Dependencies: disabling either switch would remove all meal coverage and would very likely worsen the afternoon and evening hyperglycemia; the appropriate levers are the sensitivity factor and the SMB interval. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: smb_always_enabled true makes the COB-related switches functionally inert, and they are doubly inert because no carbohydrates were entered; there is no internal contradiction in the group. The high-temporary-target gate did suppress SMB during 180-minute targets of 135 mg/dL on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18, accounting for roughly 435 minutes out of 336 hours. Uncertainty: that exposure explains part of the elevation on those two days but not the 14-day afternoon pattern. Dependencies: enabling SMB under high temporary targets would remove a deliberate brake in a system already showing insulin accumulation to 5.935 units, so change is unsupported. All five components have values, so verify does not apply.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=5 to 8 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: a 3-minute interval against a 5-minute CGM cadence permits a microbolus on essentially every loop cycle, and observed insulin on board reached 4.73 units on 2026-08-19 and 5.935 units on 2026-08-21 against roughly 16 to 20 units per day, with post-correction drops of minus 168 and minus 178 mg/dL in 120 minutes. Uncertainty: medium. The same overshoots are equally consistent with the 27.8 to 43 mg/dL per unit effective sensitivity at high glucose, so frequency and per-dose strength are not yet separated; in addition the declared minute caps do not appear to bound delivered SMB size in this build, since reason strings record 0.4 unit microboluses and one 1.6 unit boosted SMB against a cap implying roughly 0.17 to 0.27 units, which is why only the interval component is proposed for change and the two minute caps are left as they are. Dependencies: this must be tested strictly after and separately from the dynamic sensitivity change and the max_iob change; changing it in parallel would make the result uninterpretable. All three components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: max_iob of 25 units exceeds the entire estimated daily insulin requirement of roughly 16 to 20 units and is about four times the highest insulin on board observed, 5.935 units on 2026-08-21 at 245.7 mg/dL with an effective target of 80 and sensitivity of 27.8; no sequence of dosing in this dataset could ever have reached the limit, so it provides no practical ceiling in a system that produced 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs. The max_basal component is left unchanged because the effective ceiling is the derived maxSafeBasal of 3.0 to 4.2 U/h, confirmed twice in the logs, so 12 U/h is already non-binding and lowering it would not change delivery. Uncertainty: low for the direction, moderate for the exact value, since true total daily dose is unknown because delivered basal is not summed anywhere in the package; the candidate range is therefore deliberately set well above observed peak usage. Dependencies: this is a guard rather than a dose-calculation input, so it is the least entangled change and is sequenced first, before the sensitivity and SMB interval steps. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

suggested_value: autosens_enabled=false; dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true; autosens_raises_target=false; autosens_lowers_target=false; dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=55 to 60 %
rationale: Evidence: the four switches are internally consistent, since dynamic sensitivity supersedes autosens and both autosens target switches correctly follow autosens being disabled, so none of them is proposed for change. The adjustment factor of 70 percent, however, produces effective sensitivity from 124.0 mg/dL per unit at 69.8 mg/dL with negative insulin on board down to 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL with 5.935 units on board, roughly a two-fold swing in each direction around the flat 56 anchor, which matches the observed pattern of weak correction across the 130 to 160 mg/dL plateau and roughly double-strength dosing above 200 mg/dL followed by 41 to 56 mg/dL nadirs. Uncertainty: medium. Sampled sensitivity ratios include restraining values of 0.79 to 0.94, showing the layer is not one-directional, and only 24 of 6214 device statuses were supplied so the sensitivity values are a sample rather than a distribution; GLP-1 dosing on 2026-08-14, 08-17, and 08-20 may also have shifted true sensitivity mid-window. Dependencies: must be tested separately from the SMB interval change and after the max_iob guard, because all three act on the same overshoot evidence. All five components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: both parameters govern COB decay and meal absorption modelling, and COB was reported as 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses with carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, extended_carb_entries 0, and average_extended_carb_duration_min null, so neither value influenced a single dosing decision in the period. Uncertainty: this is a keep because change is unsupported, not because the values are validated; no evidence exists in either direction, and no absorption duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependencies: if carbohydrate logging begins as proposed, these two values, min_carbs_required_grams, the COB-related activation switches, and the carb ratio segments all become live at once, which is precisely the simultaneous dependent change the workflow forbids; they should therefore be reviewed only after several announced meals exist. Both components have values, so verify does not apply.

Evidence: local hours 00:00 to 03:00 show 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent below range, which looks like basal excess, but lows recur despite frequent zero-rate temporary basals of 10 to 55 minutes, meaning delivery was already suspended when the lows occurred. Uncertainty: the preceding evening carries a 10-hour DIA tail plus boosted UAM dosing, so the responsible insulin was delivered hours earlier. Dependencies: this row cannot be separated from dynamic ISF, max IOB and the absence of carbohydrate announcement, all of which are addressed earlier in the sequence; lowering it now would add a second simultaneous change and would probably not remove the cause.

Evidence: local hour 05:00 averages 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent in range and 4.8 percent below range, and hour 06:00 averages 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 percent in range, which is the best-performing window of the day. Uncertainty: minimal for this segment, since it sits in the only genuinely fasting-like period. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; altering a well-behaved segment would add noise to the verification of the earlier steps.

Evidence: local hours 06:00 and 07:00 average 99.5 mg/dL with 97.5 and 98.7 percent in range and only 2.5 and 1.3 percent below range. Uncertainty: an isolated 42 mg/dL at 08-21 07:19 local sits in an otherwise low-risk hour and may be a sensor artefact, so it does not support a reduction. Dependencies: this is the largest basal segment and therefore sets the observed automation clamp of 4 U/h through the daily safety multiplier of 5.0, so any change here would silently move an automation limit as well and must not be combined with automation changes.

Evidence: local hours 10:00 to 13:00 average 148.0, 132.3, 141.3 and 135.0 mg/dL with time above range from 7.5 to 20.2 percent, which could suggest under-basalisation. Uncertainty: no carbohydrate was entered in the period, so unannounced breakfast and midday eating is at least as plausible an explanation as the basal rate, and the loop already responds with temporary basals up to 2.7 U/h in this window. Dependencies: separating these two explanations requires the carbohydrate logging step first; a basal increase now would also raise insulin exposure ahead of the 18:00 to 19:00 low window.

Evidence: local hour 16:00 is the highest of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent above range and zero percent below range, and it coincides exactly with the lowest scheduled basal segment. Uncertainty: this coincidence is not attributable to the basal rate, because automation already reaches its maxSafeBasal clamp of 4 U/h in this window, so additional scheduled basal would be partly redundant, and unannounced afternoon eating remains an equally plausible driver. Dependencies: the constraint that no change may increase insulin exposure between 14:00 and 03:00 local applies directly here, since this window feeds the 18:00 to 19:00 low period with 15.3 percent below range; the fasting observation named in profile_recommendation must resolve this first.

Evidence: local hour 18:00 shows 7.7 percent below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and the step up from 0.5 to 0.6 U/h occurs at this boundary. Uncertainty: the level-2 clusters on 08-13 and 08-14 both began in this hour but followed high-glucose afternoons with boosted SMB and temporary basal, so the causal insulin was delivered earlier and is carried by the 10-hour DIA tail rather than by this segment. Dependencies: reducing this row would treat a symptom of the upstream accumulation identified in the automation stages and would confound the verification of the max IOB step.

Evidence: local hour 19:00 has the highest low-glucose exposure of the day at 15.3 percent below range with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, while averaging 105.4 mg/dL. Uncertainty: as in the 18:00 segment, zero-rate temporary basals were frequently already active when these lows occurred, which points to insulin-on-board of 4.7 to 5.9 U rather than to the scheduled rate. Dependencies: this is the strongest single candidate for a later basal reduction, but only if low glucose in this hour persists after carbohydrate logging and the max IOB review; changing it now would violate the one-change-at-a-time rule and mask which step produced any improvement.

Evidence: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty and COB is zero in all 24 sampled loop statuses, so this ratio was never applied to any dose during the period. Uncertainty: complete, since no observation exists that could support or refute the value. Dependencies: blocked by the meal_ecarbs_absorption stage; it becomes assessable only after the carbohydrate logging step produces paired carbohydrate and glucose data.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entry exists in the period and COB is zero throughout, so this segment was never exercised. Uncertainty: complete; the 04:00 to 08:00 window is also the quietest eating period, so it will be the last segment to gain evidence. Dependencies: requires carbohydrate logging before any assessment is possible.

Evidence: the morning rise from 99.5 mg/dL at 07:00 to 148.0 mg/dL at 10:00 local is consistent with unannounced breakfast, but with zero carbohydrate entries this ratio never acted on it. Uncertainty: dawn physiology and unannounced eating cannot be separated, and there is zero percent below range in these hours, so no safety pressure exists. Dependencies: assessment requires the carbohydrate logging step and, if breakfast is the recurring occasion chosen, this is the segment most likely to gain evidence first.

Evidence: this is the strongest ratio in the schedule and it aligns with the highest-glucose window at 16:00 local (162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range), yet it was never applied because no carbohydrate was announced. Uncertainty: complete regarding the ratio itself; the window's behaviour is currently explained by reactive UAM dosing rather than by any carbohydrate calculation. Dependencies: blocked by the absence of carbohydrate entries, and any future evaluation must also account for the low-glucose constraint in the following hours.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entry exists, so this segment never contributed to a dose; the evening pattern is dominated instead by carried insulin-on-board and small manual corrections such as 0.05 U at BG 245 with 5.94 U already on board on 08-21.
