rationale: Evidence: the unannounced-meal cap of 20 basal minutes exceeds the standard 15 basal minutes, and since carbohydrates are never announced the larger speculative cap is the only one that applies, which points the wrong way against 15.3 percent time below range at 19:00 local. The 3 minute interval is not the binding rate limiter because CGM cadence is 5.0 minutes and loop cycles follow the CGM. Uncertainty: high on effect size, because the variant delivered above the configured standard bolus cap in documented cycles, microbolusing 0.4 U against a standard maximum bolus of 0.2 U on 08-07 and 1.6 U under a high boost on 08-19, so tightening the cap may achieve less than the setting implies. Dependencies: this changes routine delivery, unlike the ceilings, so it is deliberately deferred to a later separate round after the insulin on board ceiling has been observed; keep now rather than change so that no two dependent delivery settings move together.

Evidence: both ceilings are inert. The loop capped an adjusted request of 5.9 U/h at a maximum safe basal of 4 U/h on 08-14, so 12 U/h never bound anything and 4 U/h reproduces the ceiling already in force. The 25 U insulin on board limit exceeds a full day of insulin, given 275.95 U over fourteen days and a 16.2 U per day scheduled basal, while the highest observed insulin on board was 5.935 U at 245 mg/dL and 4.73 U at 262 mg/dL, both with zero carbohydrates on board; a limit of 8 U would therefore not have blocked any dosing observed in this period while bounding the accumulation that preceded 234 to 56 mg/dL within 120 minutes on 08-14, 264 to 96 within 120 minutes on 08-19 and 206 to 53 within 180 minutes on 08-16. Uncertainty: the suggested values are candidates for care-team review, not prescriptions, and the appropriate insulin on board ceiling depends on the individual largest meal bolus plus basal accumulation, which cannot be derived here because no meal boluses exist in the data. Dependencies: none blocking, which is precisely why this is sequenced first; it is behaviourally neutral for the observed period and therefore creates a clean baseline before any delivery or profile change. The two components should still be introduced one at a time.

Evidence: the configuration is internally coherent, with one sensitivity path rather than two, and with Autosens off the target adjustment flags are correctly inert. A sensitivity ratio of 1 in most statuses is a neutral current adjustment and not evidence of anything disabled; the values 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 occur on hypo-guard cycles and are consistent with the dynamic path working. The delivered sensitivity nevertheless spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U, roughly twice as strong as the profile value at high glucose and about half as strong in the normal range, which matches the observed slow climb and abrupt fall. Uncertainty: high and bidirectional, because lowering the adjustment factor would reduce the high-glucose over-correction and help the 5.1 percent time below range but would simultaneously weaken the already slow 100 to 150 mg/dL response and worsen the 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 local. Dependencies: coupled to the flat profile sensitivity of 56 mg/dL/U and to the boost behaviour, so three inputs feed one outcome; this may be reopened only after the ceiling change has been observed, and then only instead of, never together with, a profile sensitivity change. Verify is not available because all five components are non-null.

Evidence: both values are present and conventional, and both were inert for the entire period because carbohydrate entries are zero, extended carbohydrate entries are zero, carb_treatment_entries is empty and carbohydrates on board were zero in every supplied loop status, so neither parameter influenced a single dosing decision. Uncertainty: no observational basis exists to tune either value, and no duration is inferred from any aggregate, since the average extended carbohydrate duration field is null. Dependencies: relevance is blocked by the absence of carbohydrate logging rather than by any data-quality defect; this group becomes assessable only once meals are announced, so keep is used rather than change or verify, and verify is unavailable because both components are non-null.

Evidence: the 00:00 to 02:00 local hours carry the highest low-glucose exposure of the day at 18.5 and 10.1 percent, which superficially implicates this segment, but glucose recovers from a 90.6 mg/dL nadir at 01:00 to 101.9 at 02:00 and 104.7 at 03:00 while this same rate remains in force, and 03:00 to 05:00 shows only 3.0 and 4.8 percent below range. A fixed basal excess would produce continued decline rather than self-recovery. Sampled overnight temp basals swing both ways, including 0 U/h and 1.984 U/h, so the loop is not systematically suppressing this segment. Uncertainty: the temp basal sample is 30 records and is not duration-weighted, and no per-hour insulin on board series exists. Dependencies: the competing explanation is carry-over of evening insulin, which the maximum IOB change is designed to test; this segment must not be changed in the same window as that automation change.

Evidence: the 05:00 local hour shows 95.2 percent time in range with zero percent above range and 4.8 percent below range, and the surrounding 03:00 to 08:00 block is the best-controlled part of the day. There is no directional signal supporting either an increase or a decrease. Uncertainty: the modest 4.8 percent low exposure could reflect residual overnight insulin rather than this segment. Dependencies: protected by the safety constraint that no proposal may increase net insulin between 19:00 and 03:00 local, and by the decision to keep the adjacent 00:00 segment unchanged so that any future signal remains attributable.

Evidence: the 06:00 and 07:00 local hours show 97.5 and 98.7 percent time in range with zero percent above range and 2.5 and 1.3 percent below range, the strongest control of any window, indicating this dawn rate is well matched. Uncertainty: a single 42 mg/dL extreme was recorded at 07:19 local on 2026-08-21, but one event within a window of 98.7 percent time in range does not establish a segment defect and could reflect residual insulin or sensor behaviour. Dependencies: none that would justify change; this segment is explicitly protected in the implementation order.

Evidence: the 09:00 to 11:00 local rise from 132.9 to 148.0 to 132.3 mg/dL crosses the 0.8 to 0.7 step and reaches 20.2 percent above range at 10:00, but low exposure is only 0 to 1.2 percent, and with zero carbohydrate entries an unannounced eating occasion is at least as plausible an explanation as a basal defect. A pattern is not labelled a profile defect while meals remain a plausible cause. Uncertainty: the rise cannot be separated from food without carbohydrate logging. Dependencies: resolution depends on the carbohydrate logging observation; only after announced meals exist can this segment be assessed.

Evidence: the 16:00 local hour is the worst of the day at 162.8 mg/dL average with 32.1 percent above range, and this is the lowest basal segment, which superficially suggests it is too low. This is not adopted because the following hours fall to 124.2 and 105.4 with 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range, showing that afternoon insulin does arrive and does so in excess and late. Raising this segment would most plausibly deepen the evening lows and would violate the safety constraint against increasing insulin before 19:00 to 03:00 exposure is resolved. Uncertainty: the afternoon highs are strongly confounded by unannounced eating and by GLP-1 dosing on three days. Dependencies: this segment can only be reassessed after carbohydrate logging separates meal effects from basal effects.

Evidence: the 18:00 local hour shows 7.7 percent below range with 11.9 percent above range and an average of 124.2 mg/dL, a mixed picture in which glucose is descending steeply from the afternoon peak. The low exposure here is attributed to insulin delivered earlier at the peak rather than to this basal rate, since a 0.2 U logged bolus preceded a 178 mg/dL fall on 2026-08-14 that the dose cannot explain at any sensitivity in the observed range. Uncertainty: a small contribution from this segment cannot be excluded without a duration-weighted temp basal series. Dependencies: attribution rests on the stacking hypothesis being tested by the maximum IOB change; reassess only afterwards.

Evidence: the 19:00 local hour carries 15.3 percent below range with an average of 105.4 mg/dL and minimum of 41 mg/dL, the second worst low window of the day, and this segment steps up from 0.6 to 0.7 U/h. A reduction is nonetheless withheld because the observed falls are far larger than any basal rate could produce, with two windows showing 168 and 178 mg/dL drops in 120 minutes following 0.65 U and 0.2 U logged boluses, indicating automated delivery rather than basal as the driver. Changing basal now would confound the maximum IOB observation. Uncertainty: this is the profile segment with the strongest residual case for a future reduction if the automation change proves insufficient. Dependencies: explicitly queued as the next candidate after the maximum IOB change is evaluated, as a single isolated change.

Evidence: no carbohydrate has been logged in fourteen days, with carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0 and COB reported as 0 in every sampled loop status, so this segment has no supporting or refuting evidence. A roughly 2 percent offset was noted between this profile value and the value 13.3 appearing in loop reason strings within this window, which is too small and too uncertain in origin to act on. Uncertainty: complete. The 24 therapy response windows are all correction boluses and cannot be used to derive a carb ratio, as shown by 0.2 U doses producing 120-minute changes from plus 77 to minus 178 mg/dL. Dependencies: unblocked only by the carbohydrate logging observation.

Evidence: this value was confirmed as active by loop reason strings reporting CR 11.1 at local times within this segment, which validates that the profile is running, but zero carbohydrate entries mean the value itself is unvalidated for adequacy. Uncertainty: complete with respect to correctness. Dependencies: assessment requires logged carbohydrates within the 04:00 to 08:00 local window, which do not exist; no change may be inferred from correction bolus behaviour.

Evidence: this segment covers the 09:00 to 11:00 local rise where an unannounced eating occasion is most strongly suspected, and the value was confirmed active in loop reason strings. However, with zero carbohydrate entries there is no basis to judge whether 13.2 g/U is correct. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: this is the highest-priority segment to unblock, and it is the specific target of the recommended carbohydrate logging observation for the eating occasion preceding the 09:00 to 11:00 rise.

Evidence: this is the most aggressive carb ratio in the profile and it spans the worst hyperglycaemia hour at 16:00 and the worst evening low hour at 19:00, but it is entirely inactive in practice because no carbohydrate has ever been entered, so it has contributed nothing to the observed pattern. Uncertainty: complete with respect to correctness; certain with respect to non-involvement in the observed data. Dependencies: relevant only if carbohydrate logging begins in the afternoon window, at which point its aggressiveness should be reviewed against the existing evening low pattern before use.

Evidence: confirmed active in loop reason strings at local times within this segment, but unvalidated because no carbohydrate has been logged. This segment overlaps the 22:00 to 03:00 low window, where five correction windows drifted low by 180 to 240 minutes, but those were corrections and not meal boluses, so they carry no information about this carb ratio. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: any future use in this window must account for the existing overnight low pattern and the carry-over mechanism under test.

Evidence: with dynamic sensitivity enabled and Autosens disabled, this flat value functions as a seed rather than the operative sensitivity. Observed variable sensitivity spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit, so effective insulin action is weaker than 56 near target and roughly twice as strong at 245 to 262 mg/dL. Changing the seed would be non-linearly rescaled by dynamic ISF, most strongly at the high end where the falls that produced lows originated. Uncertainty: the exact relationship between this seed and variable sensitivity in this modified fork is unconfirmed. Dependencies: this parameter and dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent are mutually confounding and must never be changed together; both are held while the maximum IOB change is evaluated first.

Evidence: the declared 90 mg/dL cannot be treated as the operative target, because effective targets observed in loop statuses ranged from 80 to 116 mg/dL while both autosens_raises_target and autosens_lowers_target are false, and user temporary targets explain only part of that range. Raising this target is a plausible response to the 18.5 percent low exposure at 01:00 local, but it cannot be justified while the algorithm is modulating targets independently and while the carry-over hypothesis is untested. Uncertainty: high, because the source of the autonomous target modulation is undocumented fork logic. Dependencies: revisit only after the maximum IOB change, and only if overnight low exposure persists.

Evidence: this daytime target spans both the 13:00 to 18:00 high block and the 18:00 to 20:00 low block, so no single directional change would improve both. Observed effective targets within this period included 80, 87, 99, 104, 106, 108 and 116 mg/dL, confirming the declared value is not what the algorithm used. Uncertainty: high; the same undocumented target modulation applies. Dependencies: any target discussion is subordinate to resolving the timing of afternoon insulin, which depends on the carbohydrate logging observation.

Evidence: the 23:00 local hour shows 88.7 percent time in range with 10.1 percent below range and only 1.2 percent above range, and glucose is already descending from the evening. This is consistent with carried-over insulin rather than with the target value itself, since the descent begins before this segment starts. Uncertainty: a higher overnight target is a reasonable future safety lever, but it cannot be separated from the carry-over mechanism at present. Dependencies: assess only after the maximum IOB change, and never simultaneously with a basal or ISF change.

Evidence: 10 hours is long, but it is not refutable from these data and it is not implicated in the observed lows. Several therapy response windows show meaningful change at 360 minutes, including minus 176, minus 70 and minus 66 mg/dL, which is weakly consistent with long action, though every one of those windows is confounded by concurrent temp basal and unannounced food. Mechanistically a long DIA raises computed insulin on board, which restrains rather than increases dosing. Uncertainty: high, because the insulin peak time for the free_peak_oref insulin type is absent from the package, so the insulin on board curve cannot be reconstructed. Dependencies: shortening DIA would raise apparent dosing headroom and would directly counteract the maximum IOB guardrail, so it must not be changed alongside it.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries and COB reported as 0 in every sampled status, UAM is the sole meal-handling mechanism and is delivering 86.0 percent time in range on entirely unannounced eating. UAM is treated strictly as unannounced-rise detection; because COB is always 0, no duplicate carbohydrate counting can occur and none is assumed. Disabling either switch would convert the 13:00 to 18:00 block, already at 22.6 to 32.1 percent above range, into a substantially larger one. Uncertainty: both components have concrete values so verify is not permissible; the residual uncertainty concerns the fork boost logic layered on top, not these switches. Dependencies: all SMB sizing and stacking questions are handled through the delivery and safety limit groups rather than by disabling the mechanism.

Evidence: the group is internally coherent. smb_always_enabled true logically dominates the two carbohydrate-conditional switches, and with zero carbohydrates those switches are inert rather than contradictory. smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false meaningfully suppresses SMB during the five recorded 135 mg/dL temporary targets, including two 180-minute windows on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18, and this is a coherent manual brake consistent with the crash history rather than a defect. Uncertainty: all five components have concrete values so verify is not permissible; the suppression behaviour means those two afternoons must be excluded from SMB sizing evidence. Dependencies: if carbohydrate logging begins, the carbohydrate-conditional switches and the 20 gram minimum become live and should be reviewed then, before any change here.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: both caps are already below AAPS defaults of 30 and 30, and the 3-minute interval matches the 5-minute CGM cadence appropriately. The caps reconcile arithmetically with the data, yielding roughly 0.23 U at 0.7 U/h basal against a reported standard maximum bolus of 0.2 U, and 0.27 U at 0.8 U/h against a reported 0.3 U. However, they are not the operative ceiling: one status delivered 0.4 U against a 0.2 U standard maximum and another delivered 1.6 U under UAM High Boost, with boost multipliers observed from 0.24 to 35.93. Reducing the UAM cap from 20 to 15 would scale only the boost base and would carry a clear cost against the existing 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 with zero percent below range in that hour. Uncertainty: all three components have concrete values so verify is not permissible; the effect size of any cap change is unpredictable because fork boost logic overrides it. Dependencies: this is the third-ranked stacking limiter and must be considered only after the maximum IOB change has been observed for a full window, never simultaneously with it or with the dynamic ISF factor.

suggested_value: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h unchanged; max_iob_units reduced from 25 U to a care-team-agreed ceiling clearly above routine operating IOB and far below 25 U, for example in the region of 8 to 10 U if total daily dose is confirmed near 20 U per day
rationale: Evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 is non-binding and is left unchanged, because the effective ceiling comes from the daily safety product, shown by a status reporting an adjusted required rate of 5.9 reduced to maxSafeBasal 4, with the highest enacted rate anywhere in the sample being 3.6 U/h. max_iob_units of 25 is the weak link: profile basal is 16.2 U per day and total_insulin_u averages 19.7 U per day, so 25 U permits approximately a full day of insulin to be simultaneously active. Sampled peaks reached 4.73 U immediately before a fall from 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes, and 5.935 U at 245 mg/dL while a further 2.12 U was still being requested at a variable sensitivity of 27.8 mg/dL per unit. This bounds the stacking mechanism implicated in the 18:00 to 20:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 low windows without altering routine dosing. Uncertainty: only 24 of 6214 statuses were sampled so 5.935 U is a floor rather than a true peak, and it is unresolved whether total_insulin_u includes basal delivery, which changes estimated total daily dose between roughly 20 and 36 U per day and therefore the appropriate ceiling; the exact value must be set by the care team against the actual total daily dose. Dependencies: this is ranked first precisely because it is the only stacking limiter adjustable without confounding basal, ISF, target or SMB sizing; it must not be combined with the dynamic ISF factor, the UAM cap, or any profile change.

Evidence: the group is internally consistent. An earlier inference in this analysis, that non-unity sensitivity ratios of 0.79 to 0.98 proved hidden Autosens activity, is withdrawn: with dynamic sensitivity enabled those ratios arise from the dynamic sensitivity path, and a ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment rather than evidence of disabled Autosens. Dynamic ISF is the de facto sensitivity engine, with observed variable sensitivity spanning 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL per unit against a flat profile seed of 56. A reduction of the adjustment factor would act as a global gain reduction, weakening insulin at every glucose level, and would be expected to worsen the existing 32.1 percent above range at 16:00 while only partially addressing the lows, because the timing analysis indicates insulin arrives late rather than being excessive in total. Uncertainty: all five components have concrete values so verify is not permissible; the direction and implementation of the adjustment factor in this modified fork is unconfirmed, which is an additional reason to withhold. Dependencies: mutually confounding with the profile ISF seed and with the maximum IOB change; revisit only after carbohydrate logging has produced 7 to 10 days of announced meals so that timing and gain can be separated.

Evidence: both parameters act on COB decay and deviation accounting, and COB was reported as 0 in every sampled loop status across fourteen days with zero grams of carbohydrate logged, so they are functionally inert in this dataset and no evidence can support a change. Both values have concrete current values, so keep is used rather than any missing-data status and verify is not permissible. One forward-looking observation is recorded rather than acted on: every observed unannounced rise rate, between 1.6 and 7.3 mg/dL per 5 minutes, sits below the 8 mg/dL threshold, so if carbohydrate logging begins, COB would be assumed to decay faster than real absorption appears to proceed. Uncertainty: the rise rates were derived from correction bolus windows confounded by insulin action, so they are indicative only and not a measurement of carbohydrate absorption. Dependencies: this group becomes evaluable only after the carbohydrate logging observation produces non-zero COB, and it should be re-checked before, not alongside, any extended carbohydrate use.

The 00:00-05:00 local block shows time below range of 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent at hours 23, 1, 2 and 3 local with means of 93.3, 90.6, 101.9 and 104.7 mg/dL and spontaneous recovery by 04:00, which is a real pattern. However, the evidence does not separate three competing causes: an insulin tail under the 10-hour DIA, the 0.6 U/h basal itself, and the tight 90 mg/dL target that leaves no buffer. Delivered temp basal in this window ranged from 0 to nearly 2 U/h in the sample, so the hourly average does not measure the scheduled rate. Uncertainty is further raised by IOB peaks of 2.80 and 5.935 U late in the evening. This segment is dependent on the outcome of the UAM delivery change and cannot be adjusted at the same time.

The 05:00-06:00 local window performs well, with a mean of 104.2 mg/dL, 95.2 percent time in range, 4.8 percent time below range and no time above range. There is no evidence of a defect, and any change here would risk the best-controlled part of the day. Uncertainty is low for this segment; the only caveat is that the isolated 42 mg/dL at 07:19 local on 08-21 sits nearby, which is monitored rather than acted upon. No dependency requires a change.

The 06:00-10:00 local block is the strongest of the day, with means of 99.5, 99.5, 110.5 and 132.9 mg/dL and time in range of 97.5, 98.7, 98.2 and 91.1 percent, with time below range of 2.5, 1.3, 0.0 and 0.0 percent. This segment is validated by the data and should be preserved as a reference for the rest of the analysis. The only uncertainty is that the 09:00-10:00 local rise begins here and may be meal-related, which cannot be resolved without carbohydrate entries.

The 10:00-16:00 local block shows rising means from 148.0 to 162.8 mg/dL with time above range from 20.2 to 32.1 percent, which could suggest insufficient basal. However, carb_entries is 0 and COB is 0 in all sampled statuses, so unannounced meals are at least as plausible, and delivered temp basal in this window reached 2.7 to 4.0 U/h, several times the scheduled rate, which means the loop was not constrained by this segment. Raising basal here would also add insulin upstream of the 18:00-19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster, which is the opposite of the current safety priority. Dependent on carbohydrate visibility and on the UAM change before reassessment.

This segment coincides with the worst hyperglycemia of the day, 162.8 mg/dL mean and 32.1 percent time above range at 16:00 local, while carrying the lowest scheduled rate of the profile, which makes it the most tempting change in the package. It is withheld for three reasons: unannounced meals explain the same rise with zero carbohydrate entries, the loop already overrode this segment with temp basals up to 4.0 U/h and was clamped at maxSafeBasal on 08-14, and increasing insulin here would feed directly into the 18:00-19:00 local hypoglycemia cluster with minima of 41 and 42 mg/dL. It is also the segment most likely to have been set low deliberately for unrecorded afternoon activity. This is the highest-priority profile candidate for reassessment once the UAM change and carbohydrate logging are in place.

This segment adds basal into a falling limb: means drop from 148.9 to 124.2 mg/dL at 18:00 local with 7.7 percent time below range and a minimum of 42 mg/dL, and two of the three level-2 episodes occur at 18:00-19:15 local. A reduction is therefore directionally plausible. It is withheld because the leading explanation is the insulin tail from afternoon UAM dosing under a 10-hour DIA rather than the scheduled 0.6 U/h, evidenced by falls of 178 and 125 mg/dL after user doses of 0.2 U, and because changing this segment simultaneously with the UAM delivery change would make neither effect interpretable. This is the second profile candidate for reassessment if the evening hypoglycemia persists after the automation step.

The 19:00 local hour carries the highest time below range of the entire day at 15.3 percent with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, while the scheduled basal rises to its joint-highest daytime value. This is a genuine mismatch in direction. The change is withheld for the same reason as the 18:00 segment: the 08-14 sequence of 234 to 200 to 56 mg/dL after a 0.2 U dose shows automation, not scheduled basal, driving the fall, and the two settings must not be changed together. If the evening cluster survives the UAM reduction, this segment and the 18:00 segment become the primary review targets, one at a time.

This carb ratio was never exercised during the period: carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty and COB is 0 in all 24 sampled loop statuses, so the value appears only as profile read-back inside loop reason strings. There is no evidence in either direction, so keep is the correct status rather than any change. Dependent on carbohydrate logging becoming available before any assessment is possible.

No carbohydrate was entered at any time in the 14-day window, so this segment produced no dosing and cannot be validated or refuted. The 04:00-08:00 local window is in any case the best-controlled part of the day on basal alone. Keep, dependent on future carbohydrate entries.

Unvalidatable for the same reason: zero carbohydrate entries and COB 0 throughout mean this ratio never contributed insulin. The morning rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL between 08:00 and 10:00 local was handled entirely by UAM, so it carries no information about the carb ratio. Keep, dependent on carbohydrate logging.

This is the strongest carb ratio in the profile and covers the worst hyperglycemia block, but with zero carbohydrate entries it was never applied, so the 32.1 percent time above range at 16:00 local says nothing about its correctness. No change is supportable. Keep, dependent on carbohydrate logging for the recurring afternoon meal, which is the designated next observation.

Never exercised during the period, as with all other carb-ratio segments. The evening pattern in this window is dominated by the falling limb from the afternoon and by insulin tail effects, not by carbohydrate dosing. Keep, dependent on carbohydrate logging.

The single flat ISF segment is not used directly, because dynamic sensitivity is enabled with a 70 percent adjustment factor and rescaled the effective value across a 4.5-fold range from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit in the sampled statuses. This makes the profile ISF and the dynamic-ISF adjustment factor partially interchangeable levers on the same output, so changing this value now would confound the planned automation observation and it is explicitly excluded from being changed together with the sensitivity group. There is also a material safety consideration: at the terminal status, 5.935 U of IOB implies a fall of about 165 mg/dL at the dynamic value of 27.8 but about 332 mg/dL at the profile value of 56, so the correct choice between the two levers requires the post-change observation. Keep for now; this is the designated third decision point in the sequence.

A target of 90 mg/dL through the 00:00-08:00 local block is tight and coincides with 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent time below range in the first hours, which makes a small increase directionally plausible. It is withheld because the same overnight pattern is equally explained by the 10-hour insulin tail from evening automation, because the 04:00-08:00 portion of the same segment performs excellently at 95.2 to 98.7 percent time in range, and because a target change would alter loop behaviour at the same time as the planned UAM change. Dependent on the outcome of that observation.

The 100 mg/dL daytime target applies across both the best-performing morning hours and the worst afternoon hours, so the hourly data give no consistent signal about it. Effective targets in the sampled statuses already varied between 80 and 116 mg/dL, and the user applied 135 mg/dL temporary targets six times, which is a more flexible instrument than a standing target change and is already in use. No change is supportable; dependent on the automation observation.

The 23:00 local hour shows 11.4 percent time below range with a mean of 105.7 mg/dL, and this segment sets a 90 mg/dL target immediately before the deepest overnight cluster, so it is a plausible contributor. It is withheld because the cause is not separated from the insulin tail and the 0.6 U/h basal that begins one hour later, and because changing the target and the UAM strength together would be uninterpretable. This segment is reassessed together with the 00:00 basal segment after the automation observation.

A 10-hour DIA is long and is a plausible contributor to the prolonged declines observed at 240 to 360 minutes after very small doses, such as 125 to 57 mg/dL at 240 minutes and 75 mg/dL at 360 minutes on 08-17, and 206 to 53 mg/dL at 180 minutes on 08-16. However, those windows contain concurrent temp basal and microbolus delivery, so they demonstrate net system action rather than the insulin curve, and no insulin peak time is supplied in the package despite insulin_type free_peak_oref, so the DIA and peak pairing cannot be validated. A longer DIA is also conservative for IOB accounting, meaning a reduction could increase rather than decrease dosing. No change is supportable on this evidence; dependent on the peak time being clarified with the care team.

Both components are present and non-null, so verify is not applicable. With zero carbohydrate entries and COB 0 in every sampled status, UAM is the only mechanism covering meals, and disabling either switch would leave every rise uncovered and would predictably worsen the 13:00-17:00 local block that already runs at 16.6 to 32.1 percent time above range. The identified problem is delivery gain, not the existence of SMB or UAM, and the gain is addressed in the delivery group instead. Uncertainty is low for this decision; the dependency is that the delivery group change must be the one that carries the effect.

All five components are non-null, so verify is not applicable. The group is internally consistent: smb_always_enabled true currently supersedes smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false, which are therefore inert while no carbohydrates are entered, and smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false gives the user a working manual brake that was used six times through 135 mg/dL temporary targets, including two 180-minute periods. No component change is supported by the data. The dependency to note is that the two currently inert flags become active as soon as carbohydrate logging begins, so this group must be re-examined at that point rather than assumed unchanged.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=15 min
rationale: Only one component is proposed for change: max_uam_smb_basal_minutes from 20 min to 15 min. Evidence: UAM is the sole meal-handling path, and observed microboluses exceeded the computed cap in this non-stock build, with 0.4 U delivered against a stated standardMaxBolus of 0.2 U under UAM Boost values of 1.23 and 1.57, and a high-boost microbolus of 1.6 U issued while IOB was already 4.73 U. Downstream consequences are falls of 178, 168 and 125 mg/dL after user doses of 0.65 U or less, guard predictions of -4 and -59 mg/dL with 120-minute zero temporary basals, IOB peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U with COB 0, and evening time below range of 7.7 and 15.3 percent with minima of 41 and 42 mg/dL. Because the UAM minute setting scales the base that the boosts multiply, the change acts proportionally and specifically on the UAM path and leaves the excellent 04:00-08:00 local window largely untouched. Uncertainty: the build-specific boost multipliers are not documented in the package, so the magnitude is approximate and must be verified empirically, and afternoon time above range may increase. Dependencies: smb_interval_minutes of 3 min is never binding against a 5-minute CGM cadence and stays unchanged, max_smb_basal_minutes of 15 min governs the non-UAM path and stays unchanged, and this change must not be combined with any sensitivity, ISF, basal or target change.

Both components are non-null, so verify is not applicable, and both are currently non-binding, which is exactly why changing them is safe and comes first. Evidence: the highest observed IOB is 5.935 U against a ceiling of 25 U, and the effective basal ceiling is already 4.0 U/h, derived from the highest profile basal of 0.8 U/h multiplied by max_daily_safety_multiplier 5, confirmed by the observed clamp of a required 5.9 U/h to maxSafeBasal 4 on 08-14, so the configured 12 U/h never engages. Proposed direction: reduce max_iob_units from 25 U to 10 U, which remains comfortably above the observed peak of 5.935 U and therefore does not alter routine dosing, and afterwards align max_basal_u_per_hour from 12 U/h to 5 U/h, which remains above the effective 4.0 U/h clamp. Rationale for containment: at the terminal status the safety of 5.935 U of IOB depends entirely on the dynamic sensitivity estimate of 27.8 mg/dL per unit being correct, and on 08-14 a comparable estimate failed, producing a fall to 56 mg/dL. Uncertainty: it is not stated whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 U includes basal delivery, so the ceiling relative to total daily dose cannot be computed precisely, which is why the proposed values sit well above observed operation. Dependency: change the two components one at a time, max_iob_units first, and complete both before the UAM delivery change.

All five components are non-null, so verify is not applicable. The configuration is internally coherent: autosens_enabled false with dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true is the normal dynamic-ISF arrangement, and both autosens target flags being false is consistent with autosens being off. Sensitivity_ratio values of 1 in the loop statuses are read as neutral current adjustments and not as evidence about the switch, and non-neutral ratios of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 also appear. Behaviourally, dynamic sensitivity ranged from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL per unit and was most aggressive at the highest glucose values, which is a coherent mechanism for the overshoot-then-crash cycle, so a reduction of the 70 percent factor is directionally plausible. It is withheld because the factor is a global gain knob that would also reduce insulin in the currently excellent 04:00-08:00 local window and against the 13:00-17:00 local time above range of 16.6 to 32.1 percent, and because it is partially interchangeable with profile.isf.00_00, so the two must never be changed together and the choice between them requires the post-UAM observation. Dependent on the delivery-group change being observed first.

Both components are non-null, so verify is not applicable. Both are currently inert: with carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, extended_carb_entries 0 and COB 0 in all 24 sampled statuses, the carbohydrate decay floor of 8 mg/dL per 5 minutes and the absorption expiry of 7 hours never execute, so no telemetry can support or refute either value and changing an inert parameter would only add noise. Uncertainty: meal_max_absorption_hours of 7 is above the common default, which may matter once carbohydrates are entered, but no meal-linked evidence exists and no duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependency: this group becomes assessable at the same moment that carbohydrate logging unblocks the five carb-ratio segments, and it must be re-reviewed then.

Evidence: local hours 00 to 03 show means of 90.6 to 104.7 mg/dL with time below range of 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent, which in isolation would suggest a small reduction. Uncertainty: in that window the loop already delivers zero temp basal with negative insulin on board of -0.481, -0.197 and -0.03 U, so ongoing basal delivery is not the active driver at that moment, and the lows may instead be the tail of afternoon overcorrection under a 10 h DIA. Dependencies: the primary dynamic ISF change targets the same lows, and changing both together would make neither attributable, so this segment is held for one observation cycle and becomes the next candidate if the window stays above about 8 percent below range.

Evidence: local hours 05 to 07 are the best-controlled part of the day, with means of 104.2, 99.5 and 99.5 mg/dL, at most 1.3 to 4.8 percent below range and no time above range. Uncertainty: minimal for this window; the single 42 mg/dL value at 07:19 local on 2026-08-21 precedes a sensor change the same day and may be an artefact. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; no adjustment is supported.

Evidence: local hours 06 to 09 show 99.5, 99.5, 110.5 and 132.9 mg/dL with zero to 2.5 percent below range and at most 8.9 percent above range, so there is no dawn defect and this higher morning rate appears appropriate. Uncertainty: the rise toward 09:00 could reflect either dawn effect or unannounced breakfast, and with zero carbohydrate entries these cannot be separated. Dependencies: any morning adjustment should wait until carbohydrate announcement makes meal effects visible.

Evidence: local hours 10 to 15 show means of 148.0, 132.3, 141.3, 135.0, 148.1 and 153.0 mg/dL with 7.5 to 26.3 percent above range, which superficially suggests under-basal. Uncertainty: with zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days and COB zero in every loop snapshot, this elevation is better explained by unannounced meals and late UAM response than by basal need. Dependencies: raising basal here would increase insulin exposure that continues into the 18:00 and 19:00 low window, which already carries 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range, so no increase is supported.

Evidence: 16:00 local is the highest hour of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent above range and zero percent below range, and it coincides exactly with the lowest daytime basal of 0.5 U/h. Uncertainty: the coincidence is not sufficient to prove a defect, because the same afternoons are followed by the deepest lows of the period at 18:00 and 19:00, and the low rate may be functioning as a necessary guard against them; meals in this block are entirely unannounced. Dependencies: this segment should only be reconsidered after carbohydrate announcement and after the dynamic ISF change has been evaluated.

Evidence: 18:00 local shows 7.7 percent below range with a mean of 124.2 mg/dL, and the level-2 clusters of 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-14 fall in and just after this hour. Uncertainty: those clusters follow corrections given at 14:05 and 17:20 local into high glucose, so the insulin tail rather than the basal rate is the more likely driver, and DIA of 10 h amplifies that tail. Dependencies: the primary dynamic ISF change directly targets this mechanism, so basal here is held until its effect is observed.

Evidence: 19:00 local carries the highest time below range of any hour at 15.3 percent with a mean of 105.4 mg/dL, which would isolate this segment as a candidate. Uncertainty: this hour sits directly downstream of the afternoon peak and its corrections, so it is the expected landing point of an insulin tail rather than an independent basal error, and the two cannot be separated from this data. Dependencies: held so that the single dynamic ISF change remains attributable; this hour is the primary observation target for that change.

Evidence: zero carbohydrate entries, 0.0 g total, empty carb_treatment_entries and COB zero in all 24 loop snapshots, so this ratio has never been exercised. Uncertainty: complete, since no observation exists to validate or invalidate it. Dependencies: it can only be reviewed after carbohydrate entry produces observable COB and meal responses.

Evidence: no carbohydrate has been entered in the period and no bolus wizard use is visible, with bolus_wizard_percentage at 100 percent but unused. Uncertainty: complete for this segment. Dependencies: review requires 7 to 10 days of entered carbohydrate amounts with timestamps.

Evidence: the 08:00 to 10:00 local rise from 110.5 to 148.0 mg/dL suggests morning intake, but no carbohydrate amount was ever recorded for it, so no ratio can be derived. Uncertainty: complete; the rise could also reflect dawn effect. Dependencies: this is the segment most likely to become assessable first, because the morning window carries almost no hypoglycemia and is the safest place to begin announcing carbohydrate.

Evidence: this is the strongest ratio in the profile and covers the block with the highest time above range, but with zero carbohydrate entries it has never actually been applied. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: strengthening any ratio in this block would add insulin upstream of the 18:00 and 19:00 low window, so it must not be changed before the hypoglycemia pattern is resolved.

Evidence: no carbohydrate entries exist for the evening block, and the 0.85 U entry at 21:40 local on 2026-08-20 is typed as a correction bolus with no associated carbohydrate. Uncertainty: complete. Dependencies: review requires carbohydrate entry data for evening meals.

Evidence: the profile declares one flat segment of 56 mg/dL per unit, but dynamic sensitivity is enabled at a 70 percent adjustment factor and the loop actually operated between 124 mg/dL per unit at glucose 70 and 27.8 mg/dL per unit at glucose 246, so 56 is an anchor rather than the delivered value. Uncertainty: the therapy response windows cannot be used to derive a numeric ISF, because their insulin_u field records only the discrete bolus of 0.05 to 2.4 U while SMB and temp basal delivery continues through the window, for example 0.2 U associated with a 178 mg/dL fall in 120 minutes. Dependencies: the anchor is deliberately held so that the single change to the dynamic ISF adjustment factor can be attributed; changing both at once would make the result uninterpretable.

Evidence: a target of 90 mg/dL during a window carrying 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range would normally invite a modest increase. Uncertainty: the loop demonstrably did not use the declared targets, operating at effective target_bg values from 80 to 116 mg/dL that tracked the sensitivity ratio while both autosens target flags are false and only five temporary targets exist in the period, so a profile target edit may not reach the loop as intended. Dependencies: how effective targets are derived in this build must be clarified before any target row is changed; until then the change is unsupported.

Evidence: the daytime target of 100 mg/dL is conventional and the 08:00 hour itself is well controlled at 110.5 mg/dL with zero percent below range. Uncertainty: the same conflict applies, since observed target_bg values of 80, 84, 86, 87, 99 and 104 mg/dL appear during the day and do not match the declared 100. Dependencies: no target change is proposed in this cycle; the dynamic ISF lever acts on the same overcorrection more directly.

Evidence: 23:00 local shows a mean of 105.7 mg/dL with 10.1 percent below range on this target. Uncertainty: the declared target is not the operative one, and this hour also sits downstream of the afternoon and evening insulin tail, so the target is not established as the driver. Dependencies: held together with the other two target rows for consistency, and reconsidered only if the overnight window remains low after the dynamic ISF change.

Evidence: a DIA of 10 h with insulin_type free_peak_oref keeps insulin accounted for deep into the tail and is consistent with the observed insulin on board peaks of 4.73 and 5.935 U and with falls arriving 120 to 240 minutes after dosing, such as 172 to 47 mg/dL at 240 minutes. Uncertainty: the package does not supply a peak time for the free peak model, and DIA, the dynamic ISF factor and the build-specific UAM boost terms all predict the same late-hypoglycemia signature, so they cannot be separated from this data. Dependencies: DIA is explicitly reserved for a later cycle so that the single dynamic ISF change stays attributable; shortening DIA at the same time would confound both.

Evidence: with zero carbohydrate entries in 14 days, UAM is the only mechanism providing meal coverage, and time in range is still 86.0 percent, so disabling either switch would enlarge the 09:00 to 17:00 elevated block that already reaches 32.1 percent above range at 16:00. UAM is not duplicating carbohydrate accounting, since COB is zero in all 24 loop snapshots. Uncertainty: UAM is the pathway through which the overcorrection is expressed, but the strength comes from the sensitivity and boost logic rather than from these two switches. Dependencies: both must remain enabled while the dynamic ISF change is evaluated, otherwise the afternoon pattern would change for a different reason.

Evidence: the group is internally consistent. smb_always_enabled true is the governing switch, so smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false are effectively inert at present, and the pairing of smb_with_temp_target_enabled true with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false suppresses SMB during the raised temporary targets this user actually sets, which were 135 mg/dL on four occasions. Uncertainty: on 2026-08-18 a 180-minute temporary target of 135 was active and the day still recorded 12.8 percent below range, which indicates the driver lies upstream of activation conditions rather than in them. Dependencies: this group becomes materially relevant once carbohydrate announcement begins, because with COB present the tighter 15-minute SMB cap applies instead of the 20-minute UAM cap; no change is supported before that.

current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
rationale: Evidence: these caps are already more conservative than AAPS defaults of 30 minutes, and against basal of 0.5 to 0.8 U/h they are small, with 20 minutes at 0.6 U/h giving about 0.2 U, matching the observed standardMaxBolus of 0.2. Crucially they are not the binding constraint: build-specific boost logic delivered 0.4 U against a 0.2 U standard cap on 2026-08-07 and an SMB of 1.6 U on 2026-08-19, and those multipliers are not exposed as configurable items in this package. Uncertainty: tightening the caps would scale only the base that a larger multiplier acts on, so the benefit is unpredictable while the cost, less prandial coverage in an already elevated afternoon, is likely. Dependencies: this is a competing lever for the same hypoglycemia signature as the dynamic ISF factor, and only one lever may move per cycle, so it is held; it may be revisited if the sensitivity change proves insufficient.

Evidence: max_iob of 25 U is not a practical ceiling against a profile basal of 16.2 U per day, and insulin on board reached 4.73 U on 2026-08-19 and 5.935 U on 2026-08-21 at 22:09 local, at which point the loop still requested 4 U/h with an insulin requirement of 2.12 U; loop reason strings show minimum guard values of -4, -59 and 28 mg/dL, and the largest falls of 234 to 56 and 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes followed those accumulations. A candidate of 8 U sits above the observed peak of 5.935 U, so it would not interfere with normal dosing, while capping further accumulation. max_basal is left at 12 U/h because it is already superseded by the enforced maxSafeBasal of 4 U/h visible on 2026-08-14, so changing it would have no observable effect and would only add a second simultaneous variable. Uncertainty: it is unclear whether total_insulin_u of 275.95 U includes basal delivery, so the true total daily dose is unknown and the exact ceiling must be set with the care team; on 2026-08-19 an occlusion and pump error mean recorded insulin on board may not equal delivered insulin. Dependencies: this is a guardrail rather than a dosing-strength change, but it must still be introduced as a separate step after the dynamic ISF observation window so the two effects remain distinguishable.

Evidence: this is the primary change of the cycle and only the adjustment factor component moves. Against a flat ISF anchor of 56 mg/dL per unit the loop operated at 42.5, 37.9 and 27.8 mg/dL per unit whenever glucose was high, roughly twice the declared strength precisely where overcorrection occurs, and the resulting falls of 234 to 56 mg/dL in 120 minutes, 264 to 96 mg/dL in 120 minutes and 172 to 47 mg/dL in 240 minutes feed the 18:00 and 19:00 window with 7.7 and 15.3 percent below range and the 23:00 to 03:00 window with 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range, against an overall 5.1 percent below range. Sensitivity ratios of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94 and 0.98 confirm the adaptation is active and that a ratio of 1 simply means a neutral current adjustment. The other four components are held: autosens_enabled false and dynamic_sensitivity_enabled true define which engine runs and must stay fixed while its strength is tested, and both target flags are already false.
